- Weijers, H. W. et al., “Progress in high field REBCO conductor and magnet technology,” Supercond. Sci. Technol. 27, 044001 (2014). [Application context for >20 T]

Step 7: Clear Definitions and Concepts
- Hierarchical pinning: Coexistence of c-axis correlated rods (BaCuO2) and ab-plane layered dots ((Gd,Yb)2O3) provides strong pinning over a broad angular and field range; rods suppress vortex motion for B∥c; dots enhance pinning for B near ab-plane.
- Lattice mismatch and coherence: Mismatch f = (d_inclusion − d_matrix)/d_matrix; minimized mismatch reduces misfit dislocations, enabling coherent interfaces and elastic strain accommodation, which stabilizes long, continuous rods.
- Power-law exponent α: At high fields where collective pinning dominates, Jc(B) often follows Jc ∝ B^−α; smaller α indicates slower decay with field.
- Characteristic crossover field B*: Field scale marking change in dominant pinning mechanism (e.g., from correlated to isotropic); extracted via two-component fits or local exponent analysis.
- Pinning force Fp: Fp = μ0 Jc B; Fp,max and its position indicate the efficiency and characteristic field of pinning centers.

Step 8: How Components Reinforce Conclusions
- Controlled composition series and constant texture isolate causality from composition → microstructure → performance.
- TEM/EDS/GPA provide direct evidence of rods/dots, coherence, and strain; 2D-XRD confirms rod orientation and volume fraction; these microstructural signatures correlate quantitatively with Jc(θ), α, and Fp.
- Baselines (undoped and 15% Zr-doped) ground the claims against well-established pinning architectures, demonstrating the advantage in the ultrahigh-field, 4 K regime.
- Ablations (off-optimal mismatch, thickness, oxygenation) test mechanistic hypotheses: coherent interfaces and elastic strain are necessary for long rods and low α; deviations introduce dislocations and degrade performance, validating the interface/strain-driven self-assembly strategy.

Experiment:
Step 1: Overview and Objectives
- Objective: Establish and validate a composition- and interface-tuned, hierarchical pinning architecture in Gd0.5Yb0.5Ba2Cu3O7−δ (GdYbBCO) coated conductors grown by reel-to-reel MOCVD on IBAD-MgO/Hastelloy that yields dense, coherent (011)-BaCuO2 nanorods and layered (Gd,Yb)2O3 nanodots, maximizing vortex pinning from 4–77 K and 0–>20 T. Quantify how Cu/Ba and RE/Ba atomic ratios govern BaCuO2 nanorod aspect ratio, density, and interface coherency, and how (Gd,Yb)2O3 nanodots complement ab-plane pinning. Benchmark against state-of-the-art 15% Zr-doped REBCO and undoped REBCO.
- Key targets to validate: 
  - c-axis texture Δω≈2°, in-plane texture Δφ≈4°; c-lattice parameter 11.63–11.67 Å.
  - Self-assembled (011)-BaCuO2 nanorods ≈7 nm wide, ≈52 nm long, density ≈3700 μm⁻² per layer; (Gd,Yb)2O3 nanodots 5–9 nm tilted ≤7° from ab-plane.
  - Minimized BaCuO2/REBCO lattice mismatch ≈5.6% with coherent, dislocation-free interfaces.
  - Transport Jc ≥13 MA cm⁻² at 4 K, 5 T; power-law Jc∝B^−α with α≈0.39 at high fields; B*≈0.55 T at 10 K; Fp,max≈670 GN m⁻³ at 4 K.
- Relevance: High-field magnets for fusion, accelerators, and NMR require slow Jc field decay at 4 K and >20 T; hierarchical pinning can outperform 15% Zr-doped REBCO in this regime.

Step 2: Experimental Design (rigorous plan, baselines, ablations, evaluation)
2.1 Sample set and matrix
- Substrates: Commercial IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tapes with identical architecture and texture (Δω<3°, Δφ<5°) for all samples to isolate composition effects.
- Film thickness: 0.54 ± 0.05 μm for all samples to avoid thickness-related relaxation.
- Composition space (two-stage design to limit runs while ensuring coverage):
  Stage A (Cu/Ba series at fixed RE/Ba=0.65): Cu/Ba = 1.15, 1.17, 1.19, 1.21.
  Stage B (RE/Ba series at fixed Cu/Ba=1.19): RE/Ba = 0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70, 0.75.
- Replicates: 3 independent tapes per condition (≥15 cm length each) for statistics.
- Controls/baselines:
  - Baseline-1 (No 2° phases): Stoichiometric Gd0.5Yb0.5BCO with Cu/Ba=1.00, RE/Ba=0.50 (minimize secondary phases).
  - Baseline-2 (Industry standard pinning): 15% Zr-doped GdYbBCO (BaZrO3 nanorods) grown under identical conditions and thickness.
  - Texture control: Subset grown on deliberately lower texture tapes (Δφ≈7°) at the optimal composition to quantify texture sensitivity (one sample).
- Ablations and targeted variants:
  - Interface/lattice mismatch ablation: Deviate from the optimal ratios to increase mismatch (e.g., Cu/Ba=1.17 and 1.21 at RE/Ba=0.65; RE/Ba=0.60 and 0.70 at Cu/Ba=1.19) and quantify misfit dislocation density and nanorod continuity.
  - Strain relaxation ablation: Increase film thickness to 0.9 μm at optimal composition to assess whether plastic relaxation truncates rods.
  - Oxygenation ablation: Two δ levels (fully oxygenated at 450 °C vs slightly under-oxygenated 375 °C) at the optimal composition to decouple effects of c-lattice parameter on mismatch and pinning.
2.2 Growth and processing consistency checks
- Keep substrate texture, buffer architecture, growth temperature window, total pressure, and oxygen partial pressure identical across the main matrix; adjust only Cu/Ba and RE/Ba via precursor flow control.
- Oxygenation: Apply the same post-anneal schedule to all samples unless explicitly part of an ablation.
2.3 Measurements and evaluation criteria
- Structural/texture metrics:
  - XRD (rocking curve FWHM Δω, φ-scan Δφ), c-lattice parameter from 00l reflections; target c=11.63–11.67 Å.
  - 2D-XRD at χ≈45° to resolve (011)-BaCuO2 orientation and azimuthal width; nanorod alignment quantified by azimuthal FWHM ≤10° around c-axis.
- Microstructure metrics (cross-sectional TEM on FIB lamellae):
  - Nanorod width, length, and areal density (≥100 rods per sample), continuity (fraction spanning ≥80% of film thickness), and orientation with respect to c-axis.
  - (Gd,Yb)2O3 nanodot size (5–9 nm) and layering periodicity (distance between dot layers).
  - Interface coherence: misfit dislocation line density (dislocations/μm of interface) from HRTEM; target near-zero density at optimum.
  - GPA strain maps to quantify tensile strain in BaCuO2 (~3%) and compressive strain in REBCO (~−10% to −12%) fields around rods/dots.
- Compositional metrics:
  - EDS and STEM-EDS line scans/maps to confirm BaCuO2 nanorods (Ba–Cu–O) and RE2O3 nanodots (Gd/Yb–O) composition and spatial separation.
  - ICP-OES or RBS on film scrapings from sacrificial segments to confirm Cu/Ba and RE/Ba within ±0.01–0.02 of targets.
- Superconducting/transport metrics:
  - Tc and ΔTc from 4-point resistivity; aim Tc≈88–92 K.
  - Transport Jc (1 μV cm⁻¹ criterion) at 4, 10, 20, 40, 65, 77 K and B = 0–5 T; angular dependence θ=0–180° with 2° steps.
  - Magnetization Jc (Bean model) at 4–77 K up to 14 T, calibrated against transport at overlapping conditions.
  - High-field transport or magnetization at 4.2 K up to 31–35 T for selected top performers at a high-field user facility; determine α from high-field Jc ∝ B^−α and compare to 15% Zr-doped baseline.
- Figures of merit and pass/fail thresholds:
  - Optimize for: maximal Fp,max at 4 K; minimal α at 4 K in 15–30 T; high Jc_min across angles (especially B∥c and B∥ab).
  - Quantify B* by two-component fit (correlated + isotropic pinning) and from local exponent analysis (see Step 4.5); cross-validate both methods.

Step 3: Implementation of Technologies/Methods
3.1 Reel-to-reel MOCVD growth (IBAD-MgO/Hastelloy)
- Substrates: Hastelloy tapes with buffer stack (e.g., Al2O3 seed/Y2O3/IBAD-MgO/epi-MgO or LaMnO3) providing Δω≈2°, Δφ≈4°; width 4–5 mm.
- Precursors: β-diketonate metal-organic precursors:
  - Ba(thd)2 (thd = 2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-3,5-heptanedione), Cu(thd)2, Gd(thd)3, Yb(thd)3 in separate, temperature-controlled bubblers.
  - Carrier gases: high-purity Ar/O2; water vapor addition optional for enhanced oxidation.
- Growth conditions (evidence-based ranges for REBCO MOCVD):
  - Substrate temperature: 780–820 °C, tuned to maintain epitaxy and coherent interfaces without excessive surface diffusion.
  - Total pressure: 2–10 Torr; O2 partial pressure: 0.5–3 Torr (balance Ar).
  - Tape travel speed set to achieve 0.54 μm thickness (typ. 0.3–1 μm h⁻¹ equivalent growth rate; deposition time per 15 cm sample ≈20–60 min).
  - Oxygenation: In-situ cool-down in 1 atm O2 from 500 °C, then ex-situ anneal 450 °C in flowing O2 for 30–60 min (δ optimization).
- Composition control:
  - Independently throttle Ba, Cu, and (Gd+Yb) precursor flows using mass-flow-controlled carrier gas through each bubbler. Maintain RE mixture Gd:Yb = 1:1 in the RE line.
  - Targeted Cu/Ba: 1.15–1.21; targeted RE/Ba: 0.55–0.75.
  - Calibrate delivery by quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) in a witness position and by ex-situ ICP-OES of trial films; establish transfer function from gas flow to film stoichiometry; verify stability over 3 h runs.
  - In-situ optical emission spectroscopy (if available) monitors relative metal-organic fragmentation; adjust flows to keep ratios within ±2%.
- Rationale for self-assembly:
  - Slight Cu-rich composition promotes Ba–Cu–O phase separation as BaCuO2 under supersaturation; epitaxial strain energy and minimal mismatch at targeted stoichiometry bias rod growth along c-axis, analogous to strain-driven self-assembly of BaZrO3 and RE2O3 nanorods/dots in REBCO.
- Oxygen stoichiometry and c-lattice tuning:
  - Post-anneal and quench protocols adjust δ to place c in 11.63–11.67 Å window; avoid over-oxygenation that may drive misfit changes.
3.2 Patterning and transport
- Pattern bridges 50–100 μm wide, 1–3 mm long by laser scribing or photolithography/ion milling to reduce self-heating and ensure uniform current distribution.
- Contacts: Sputtered Ag pads with low-resistance soldered leads; measure contact resistances <1 mΩ at 300 K.
- Transport measurements:
  - 4-probe, 1 μV cm⁻¹ criterion; voltage tap spacing 1–2 mm; pulsed current (10–20 ms) at 4 K and high fields to mitigate heating; DC at 77 K.
  - Rotating stage for angular Jc with 0.1° encoder; sweep θ at fixed B and fixed T; record full 0–180° due to tape symmetry.
3.3 Magnetization and high-field measurements
- PPMS/VSM up to 14 T, 4–77 K; pick-up coil calibrated with standard samples. Determine ΔM from full hysteresis loops (±B).
- Bean model for coated conductors (rectangular prism, a ≤ b, thickness t):
  - Jc = 20ΔM / [a(1 − a/3b)] for SI units with ΔM in A·m², dimensions in m; for thin tapes (t ≪ a ≪ b), use thin-film corrections; calibrate with transport Jc at 77 K, 1–3 T to fix geometry factor.
- High-field (≥20 T) at user facility:
  - Short patterned samples mounted on low-thermal-conductance stage; pulsed or DC fields up to 31–35 T at 4.2 K; if transport is impractical, use magnetization-derived Jc with prior calibration to transport on the same sample.
3.4 XRD and 2D-XRD
- Θ–2Θ scans and rocking curves for 00l to extract c and Δω; φ-scans on 103 for Δφ.
- 2D area detector at sample tilt χ≈45° to intercept (011)-BaCuO2 reflections; map azimuthal intensity to quantify rod alignment and volume fraction; collect pole figures of BaCuO2 and REBCO to check epitaxial relationships.
3.5 TEM/EDS/GPA
- FIB cross-sections with low-kV final polish to minimize damage.
- STEM-HAADF for Z-contrast imaging of nanorods/dots; EDS maps of Ba, Cu, Gd, Yb, O.
- HRTEM of rod/matrix interfaces; count misfit dislocations per μm; target near-zero at optimal composition; compare with off-optimal compositions.
- GPA on HRTEM images to quantify local strain εxx, εzz around rods and within matrix; extract average rod core tensile strain and matrix compressive strain; correlate with rod continuity and α.
3.6 Quantification of pinning and scaling analysis
- Jc(B) analysis:
  - Fit high-field region (e.g., 10–14 T magnetization; ≥15 T high-field) to Jc(B) ∝ B^−α; extract α and 95% CI.
  - Total pinning force Fp = μ0JcB; find Fp,max and the field B at Fp,max; normalize Fp to Fp,max to compare curves.
- Two-component pinning model:
  - Model Jc(B,θ) = Jc,c(B)·g_c(θ) + Jc,ab(B)·g_ab(θ) + Jc,iso(B), where g_c and g_ab describe angular kernels for correlated c-axis rods and ab-plane dots; fit angular curves at fixed T and B to deconvolve contributions.
- B* determination:
  - Method 1 (two-component crossover): Fit Jc(B) = A_c B^−α_c + A_iso B^−α_iso; define B* where the two components are equal.
  - Method 2 (local exponent): Compute αloc(B) = −d ln Jc / d ln B; define B* at the inflection or at αloc midpoint between low- and high-B asymptotes; report both and their agreement.
- Anisotropic GL scaling:
  - Apply Blatter scaling Bε(θ)=B√(cos²θ+γ⁻²sin²θ) to the isotropic background; deviations near θ≈0° and 90° quantify correlated pinning strength; extract effective mass anisotropy γ.

Step 4: Data Analysis, Result Evaluation, and How Design Validates Conclusions
4.1 Reliability and statistics
- For each condition (≥3 tapes), report mean ± standard deviation for nanorod size, density, Jc, α, Fp,max; require relative standard deviation <10% to claim robustness.
- Cross-batch validation: Prepare one repeat batch after two weeks; compare key metrics; perform t-tests (p<0.05) and report effect sizes.
- Calibration checks: Transport vs magnetization Jc agreement within 10% at overlapping T,B; if not, adjust geometry factor or correct for demagnetization.
4.2 Linking composition → microstructure → pinning
- Cu/Ba series at RE/Ba=0.65: Expect narrow optimum around Cu/Ba≈1.19 showing maximal rod density and aspect ratio, coherent interfaces (minimal misfit dislocations), strongest c-axis peak in Jc(θ), and lowest α. Off-optimal compositions should show surface CuO/RECuO2 precipitates, reduced rod continuity, increased interface defects, higher α.
- RE/Ba series at Cu/Ba=1.19: Increasing RE/Ba increases (Gd,Yb)2O3 dot density and ab-plane pinning but shortens rods and thickens diameter; an optimum at RE/Ba≈0.65 balances g_c and g_ab, maximizing Fp,max and raising B* while retaining low α.
- Interface/strain evidence: At the optimum, GPA shows elastic strain fields without plastic relaxation; off-optimal shows misfit dislocations and rod truncation; correlate misfit dislocation density with degradation in α and Fp.
4.3 Baseline and comparative evaluation
- Compare optimal GdYbBCO-BCO/RE2O3 to:
  - Undoped baseline: demonstrate orders-of-magnitude stronger angular peaks and higher Jc across 4–77 K, validating necessity of hierarchical pinning.
  - 15% Zr-doped baseline: show superior high-field (≥20 T) retention (lower α) with comparable or better Jc at 4 K; equal or higher Fp,max at 4 K; demonstrates competitiveness for ultrahigh-field magnets.
4.4 Criteria to claim success
- Structural: Δω≤3°, Δφ≤5°; c=11.63–11.67 Å; 2D-XRD confirms (011)-BaCuO2 rods aligned near c-axis; HRTEM shows largely coherent interfaces at optimal composition.
- Microstructural: Rod width 6–8 nm; length 45–60 nm; density 3000–4500 μm⁻² per layer; nanodots 5–9 nm tilted ≤7° from ab-plane.
- Superconducting: At 4 K, Fp,max≥600 GN m⁻³; α≤0.45 in 15–30 T regime; Jc(4 K, 5 T) ≥12 MA cm⁻²; angular anisotropy shows strong c- and ab-peaks consistent with bidirectional pinning; B*≥0.5 T at 10 K.
- Reproducibility: Achieve within ±10% across replicates; baselines differ as expected per literature.

Step 5: Feasibility, Resources, Timeline, and Risk Mitigation
5.1 Facilities and resources
- R2R MOCVD coater with independent Ba/Cu/RE precursor delivery; QCM; gas handling; O2 supply; oxygen anneal furnace.
- XRD with area detector; FIB; TEM/STEM-EDS with HRTEM and GPA software; SEM for thickness.
- Transport and magnetization: 77 K cryostat; 4–14 T PPMS/VSM; high-field user facility access (e.g., DC or resistive magnets up to 31–35 T).
- Personnel: 1 MOCVD process engineer, 1 thin film scientist for XRD, 1 TEM specialist, 1 low-temperature transport specialist, 1 data analyst; safety officer for MO precursors.
5.2 Timeline (approximate)
- Months 0–1: MOCVD calibration (composition-flow maps); baseline samples.
- Months 2–3: Stage A (Cu/Ba series) growth and basic characterization; down-select 2–3 best Cu/Ba.
- Months 4–5: Stage B (RE/Ba series) with best Cu/Ba; complete microstructure and transport; choose optimal composition.
- Months 6–7: Ablations (mismatch, thickness, oxygenation) and texture control; replicate optimal condition.

5.3 Risks and mitigations
- Composition drift or precursor delivery instability: Frequent calibration with ICP-OES; use mass flow stabilization and bubbler temperature controls; run short witness samples before each batch.

- Contact heating at 4 K high-field transport: Use pulsed currents, narrow bridges, and low-resistance contacts; if needed, rely on magnetization with transport calibration.
- Facility time constraints for >20 T: Pre-screen to send only top 3 samples; arrange beamtime in advance; provide both transport and magnetization options.

### **Experimental Plan: Engineering Hierarchical Pinning Landscapes in GdYbBCO Coated Conductors for Ultrahigh-Field Applications**

This experimental plan details a systematic investigation into the fabrication and characterization of Gd0.5Yb0.5Ba2Cu3O7-δ (GdYbBCO) coated conductors with self-assembled hierarchical pinning centers. The primary goal is to validate the hypothesis that precise compositional tuning of Cu/Ba and (Gd+Yb)/Ba ratios can create an optimal, coherent nanostructure of BaCuO2 (BCO) nanorods and (Gd,Yb)2O3 (REO) nanodots, leading to superior superconducting performance at low temperatures (4 K) and in ultrahigh magnetic fields (>20 T).

### **1. Experimental Design**

The experimental design is structured to systematically test the key hypotheses regarding composition-structure-property relationships. It incorporates a well-defined baseline, comparative studies across a matrix of compositions, and an ablation-style analysis to isolate the effects of different pinning mechanisms.

**Step 1: Baseline and Control Sample Preparation**
To establish a robust performance benchmark, two types of baseline conductors will be fabricated and characterized alongside the experimental samples.

*   **Baseline 1 (Industry Standard):** A 15% Zr-doped GdBCO coated conductor. This material is a well-established high-performance conductor known for its strong isotropic pinning from Gd2Zr2O7 nanoparticles. It serves as the primary benchmark for high-field performance.
    *   *Reference:* Xu, A. et al., "High-performance high-T c superconducting wires," *Nature Materials*, 13, 456–460 (2014). This work highlights the effectiveness of Zr-doping for enhancing in-field Jc.
*   **Baseline 2 (Stoichiometric Control):** A stoichiometric Gd0.5Yb0.5Ba2Cu3O7-δ conductor (i.e., RE:Ba:Cu = 1:2:3, corresponding to RE/Ba = 0.5, Cu/Ba = 1.5). This sample will be grown under identical conditions to the experimental samples but without the excess Cu and RE needed to form the secondary phase pinning centers. This control allows for the isolation of the intrinsic properties of the GdYbBCO matrix and serves as a reference to quantify the enhancement provided by the engineered nanostructures.

**Step 2: Comparative Study - Compositional Matrix Fabrication**
A matrix of GdYbBCO samples will be fabricated by systematically varying the precursor molar ratios during the MOCVD process to achieve targeted atomic ratios in the final film. All samples will be grown on identical 10 mm wide Hastelloy C276 substrates with a standard IBAD-MgO buffer layer architecture to ensure consistent texture (Δω < 3°, Δφ < 5°). The target film thickness for all samples will be 0.54 μm.

*   **Series A (Cu/Ba Variation):** Fix the RE/Ba ratio at the proposed optimum of 0.65 and vary the Cu/Ba ratio. This series is designed to test the hypothesis that Cu/Ba=1.19 is optimal for forming dense, vertically aligned BCO nanorods.
    *   Sample A1: Cu/Ba = 1.15
    *   Sample A2: Cu/Ba = 1.17
    *   **Sample A3 (Proposed Optimum): Cu/Ba = 1.19**
    *   Sample A4: Cu/Ba = 1.21
*   **Series B (RE/Ba Variation):** Fix the Cu/Ba ratio at the proposed optimum of 1.19 and vary the RE/Ba ratio. This series tests the hypothesis that RE/Ba=0.65 provides the optimal balance between BCO nanorod length and REO nanodot density.
    *   Sample B1: RE/Ba = 0.55
    *   Sample B2: RE/Ba = 0.60
    *   **Sample B3 (Proposed Optimum, identical to A3): RE/Ba = 0.65**
    *   Sample B4: RE/Ba = 0.70
    *   Sample B5: RE/Ba = 0.75

**Step 3: Ablation Study Design**
While true ablation (complete removal) of one defect type is not possible due to the co-precipitation process, this design allows for a systematic de-emphasis of one pinning mechanism relative to the other.

*   **Isolating BCO Nanorod Effects:** By comparing samples within Series A (A1-A4), where the RE/Ba ratio is constant, we can primarily attribute changes in c-axis correlated pinning (probed by Jc with B//c) to the morphology and density of the BCO nanorods. We expect Sample A3 to show the highest Jc(B//c) and the lowest power-law exponent α, indicating dominant, strong c-axis pinning.
*   **Isolating REO Nanodot Effects:** By comparing samples within Series B (B1-B5), where the Cu/Ba ratio is constant, we can study the effect of increasing REO nanodot density. The REO nanodots are expected to enhance pinning for magnetic fields oriented away from the c-axis. Therefore, angular-dependent Jc(θ) measurements will be critical. We hypothesize that as RE/Ba increases from 0.55 to 0.75, the Jc peak at B//ab will become more pronounced, even as the BCO nanorods may become less effective, potentially reducing the Jc peak at B//c.

**Step 4: Data Analysis and Result Evaluation Criteria**
A multi-faceted approach will be used to evaluate the results and validate the hypotheses.

*   **Microstructural Evaluation:**
    *   **TEM/STEM:** Quantify BCO nanorod dimensions (length, diameter), density (number per μm²), and vertical alignment. Quantify REO nanodot size and density. The optimal sample (A3/B3) is expected to have nanorods ≈7 nm wide and ≈52 nm long with a density ≈3700 μm⁻².
    *   **GPA Strain Mapping:** Measure the strain fields at the BCO/GdYbBCO and REO/GdYbBCO interfaces. Success is defined by observing coherent, dislocation-free interfaces for the optimal composition, with strain values consistent with theoretical predictions (e.g., ≈-12% compressive in the REBCO matrix around the BCO nanorods).
    *   **2D-XRD:** Confirm the (011) orientation of BCO nanorods. The intensity of the (011) BCO peak relative to the matrix peaks will be used as a proxy for the volume fraction of well-aligned nanorods.
*   **Superconducting Property Evaluation:**
    *   **Critical Current Density (Jc):** The primary metric. Jc will be measured as a function of temperature (4 K, 20 K, 40 K, 60 K, 77 K), magnetic field (0-14 T, with select samples measured >20 T), and angle (B//c to B//ab).

Each precursor will be held in an individual sublimator with precise temperature control (±0.1 °C) to regulate its vapor pressure.
*   **Gas Delivery:** Mass flow controllers will precisely meter argon (Ar) carrier gas through each sublimator. The precursor-laden gas streams will be mixed before entering the deposition chamber. A separate line will deliver the oxidant (N2O or O2).

    *   Substrate Temperature: 780 °C

**Step 2: Microstructural and Strain Characterization**
*   **TEM/STEM:** Cross-sectional TEM samples will be prepared using a Focused Ion Beam (FIB) system (e.g., FEI Helios). High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) and Scanning TEM (STEM) with a High-Angle Annular Dark-Field (HAADF) detector will be performed on a probe-corrected microscope (e.g., FEI Titan). HAADF-STEM is ideal for this system as its Z-contrast imaging will clearly distinguish the heavier Gd/Yb atoms in the matrix and REO dots from the lighter elements in the BCO nanorods.
*   **Geometric Phase Analysis (GPA):** GPA is a powerful image processing technique applied to HRTEM images to map lattice distortions.

By taking the gradient of the displacement field, a 2D map of the strain tensor components (εxx, εyy, εxy) can be generated with nanometer-scale resolution.

*   **Transport Jc:** Samples will be patterned into 2 mm long, 100 μm wide bridges using photolithography and a wet chemical etch. ### **Experimental Plan: Engineering Hierarchical Pinning Landscapes in GdYbBCO Coated Conductors for Ultrahigh-Field Applications**

This experimental plan details a systematic investigation into the fabrication and characterization of Gd0.5Yb0.5Ba2Cu3O7-δ (GdYbBCO) coated conductors with self-assembled hierarchical pinning centers. The primary goal is to validate the hypothesis that precise compositional tuning of Cu/Ba and (Gd+Yb)/Ba ratios can create an optimal, coherent nanostructure of BaCuO2 (BCO) nanorods and (Gd,Yb)2O3 (REO) nanodots, leading to superior superconducting performance at low temperatures (4 K) and in ultrahigh magnetic fields (>20 T).

### **1. Experimental Design**

The experimental design is structured to systematically test the key hypotheses regarding composition-structure-property relationships. It incorporates a well-defined baseline, comparative studies across a matrix of compositions, and an ablation-style analysis to isolate the effects of different pinning mechanisms.

**Step 1: Baseline and Control Sample Preparation**
To establish a robust performance benchmark, two types of baseline conductors will be fabricated and characterized alongside the experimental samples.

*   **Baseline 1 (Industry Standard):** A 15% Zr-doped GdBCO coated conductor. This material is a well-established high-performance conductor known for its strong isotropic pinning from Gd2Zr2O7 nanoparticles. It serves as the primary benchmark for high-field performance.
    *   *Reference:* Xu, A. et al., "High-performance high-T c superconducting wires," *Nature Materials*, 13, 456–460 (2014). This work highlights the effectiveness of Zr-doping for enhancing in-field Jc.
*   **Baseline 2 (Stoichiometric Control):** A stoichiometric Gd0.5Yb0.5Ba2Cu3O7-δ conductor (i.e., RE:Ba:Cu = 1:2:3, corresponding to RE/Ba = 0.5, Cu/Ba = 1.5). This sample will be grown under identical conditions to the experimental samples but without the excess Cu and RE needed to form the secondary phase pinning centers. This control allows for the isolation of the intrinsic properties of the GdYbBCO matrix and serves as a reference to quantify the enhancement provided by the engineered nanostructures.

**Step 2: Comparative Study - Compositional Matrix Fabrication**
A matrix of GdYbBCO samples will be fabricated by systematically varying the precursor molar ratios during the MOCVD process to achieve targeted atomic ratios in the final film. All samples will be grown on identical 10 mm wide Hastelloy C276 substrates with a standard IBAD-MgO buffer layer architecture to ensure consistent texture (Δω < 3°, Δφ < 5°). The target film thickness for all samples will be 0.54 μm.

*   **Series A (Cu/Ba Variation):** Fix the RE/Ba ratio at the proposed optimum of 0.65 and vary the Cu/Ba ratio. This series is designed to test the hypothesis that Cu/Ba=1.19 is optimal for forming dense, vertically aligned BCO nanorods.
    *   Sample A1: Cu/Ba = 1.15
    *   Sample A2: Cu/Ba = 1.17
    *   **Sample A3 (Proposed Optimum): Cu/Ba = 1.19**
    *   Sample A4: Cu/Ba = 1.21
*   **Series B (RE/Ba Variation):** Fix the Cu/Ba ratio at the proposed optimum of 1.19 and vary the RE/Ba ratio. This series tests the hypothesis that RE/Ba=0.65 provides the optimal balance between BCO nanorod length and REO nanodot density.
    *   Sample B1: RE/Ba = 0.55
    *   Sample B2: RE/Ba = 0.60
    *   **Sample B3 (Proposed Optimum, identical to A3): RE/Ba = 0.65**
    *   Sample B4: RE/Ba = 0.70
    *   Sample B5: RE/Ba = 0.75

**Step 3: Ablation Study Design**
While true ablation (complete removal) of one defect type is not possible due to the co-precipitation process, this design allows for a systematic de-emphasis of one pinning mechanism relative to the other.

*   **Isolating BCO Nanorod Effects:** By comparing samples within Series A (A1-A4), where the RE/Ba ratio is constant, we can primarily attribute changes in c-axis correlated pinning (probed by Jc with B//c) to the morphology and density of the BCO nanorods. We expect Sample A3 to show the highest Jc(B//c) and the lowest power-law exponent α, indicating dominant, strong c-axis pinning.
*   **Isolating REO Nanodot Effects:** By comparing samples within Series B (B1-B5), where the Cu/Ba ratio is constant, we can study the effect of increasing REO nanodot density. The REO nanodots are expected to enhance pinning for magnetic fields oriented away from the c-axis. Therefore, angular-dependent Jc(θ) measurements will be critical. We hypothesize that as RE/Ba increases from 0.55 to 0.75, the Jc peak at B//ab will become more pronounced, even as the BCO nanorods may become less effective, potentially reducing the Jc peak at B//c.

**Step 4: Data Analysis and Result Evaluation Criteria**
A multi-faceted approach will be used to evaluate the results and validate the hypotheses.

*   **Microstructural Evaluation:**
    *   **TEM/STEM:** Quantify BCO nanorod dimensions (length, diameter), density (number per μm²), and vertical alignment. Quantify REO nanodot size and density. The optimal sample (A3/B3) is expected to have nanorods ≈7 nm wide and ≈52 nm long with a density ≈3700 μm⁻².
    *   **GPA Strain Mapping:** Measure the strain fields at the BCO/GdYbBCO and REO/GdYbBCO interfaces. Success is defined by observing coherent, dislocation-free interfaces for the optimal composition, with strain values consistent with theoretical predictions (e.g., ≈-12% compressive in the REBCO matrix around the BCO nanorods).
    *   **2D-XRD:** Confirm the (011) orientation of BCO nanorods. The intensity of the (011) BCO peak relative to the matrix peaks will be used as a proxy for the volume fraction of well-aligned nanorods.
*   **Superconducting Property Evaluation:**
    *   **Critical Current Density (Jc):** The primary metric. Jc will be measured as a function of temperature (4 K, 20 K, 40 K, 60 K, 77 K), magnetic field (0-14 T, with select samples measured >20 T), and angle (B//c to B//ab).
    *   **Power-Law Exponent (α):** Determined from the field dependence of Jc (Jc ∝ B⁻ᵃ). A lower α value indicates slower Jc decay with field, which is critical for high-field applications. The target for the optimal sample is α ≤ 0.39 at 4 K.
    *   **Pinning Force (Fp):** Calculated as Fp = Jc × B. The maximum pinning force (Fp,max) and the irreversibility field (Birr, where Jc approaches zero) will be determined. The target for the optimal sample is Fp,max ≈ 670 GN m⁻³ at 4 K.
*   **Validation Criteria:** The research will be considered successful if the optimized sample (A3/B3) simultaneously meets the following criteria:
    1.  Demonstrates the target hierarchical microstructure (long BCO rods, dense REO dots, coherent interfaces) via TEM and GPA.
    2.  Achieves a transport Jc(4 K, 5 T, B//c) ≥ 13 MA cm⁻².
    3.  Exhibits a power-law exponent α ≤ 0.39 at 4 K in the high-field regime.
    4.  Shows a higher Jc at 4 K and fields >20 T compared to the 15% Zr-doped GdBCO baseline conductor.

Experiment:

**Experimental Design:**

Step 1: Define Baseline and Comparative Methods  
Establish a baseline using standard Gd0.5Yb0.5Ba2Cu3O7-δ (GdYbBCO) films without composition tuning, grown on IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tapes via reel-to-reel MOCVD, with default precursor ratios (Cu/Ba=1.0, RE/Ba=0.5) leading to no intentional self-assembled secondary phases. Comparative methods involve preparing a series of samples with varied Cu/Ba and RE/Ba ratios as per strategies: (a) Fix RE/Ba=0.65 and vary Cu/Ba from 1.15 to 1.21 in increments of 0.02; (b) Fix Cu/Ba=1.19 and vary RE/Ba from 0.55 to 0.75 in increments of 0.05. This allows direct comparison of microstructure and performance against the baseline to identify optimal ratios for nanorod and nanodot formation.

Step 2: Ablation Study Design  
Conduct ablation studies by selectively omitting key tuning elements: (i) Ablate composition tuning by using fixed default ratios, observing absence of nanorods/nanodots; (ii) Ablate interface tuning by intentionally introducing higher mismatch (>6.6%) via off-stoichiometric precursors, leading to dislocations; (iii) Ablate texture tuning by using substrates with poorer texture (Δω>5°, Δφ>7°); (iv) Ablate stress tuning by post-annealing samples to relax strains. Each ablation variant will be compared to the fully tuned sample to quantify the contribution of each strategy to pinning enhancement.

Step 3: Data Analysis and Result Evaluation Criteria  
Analyze microstructure data from TEM/SEM/EDS (e.g., nanorod dimensions, density, orientation) and strain from GPA, requiring statistical sampling of ≥100 nanorods per sample for reliability. For performance, measure Jc via transport (1 μV cm⁻¹ criterion) and magnetization (Bean model), fitting Jc(B) to power-law Jc ∝ B^{-α} to extract α, and calculate pinning force Fp = Jc × B. Evaluation criteria: Optimal sample must achieve Jc >10 MA cm⁻² at 4 K/5 T, α <0.4, B* >500 mT at 10 K, and Fp >600 GN m⁻³ at 4 K/5 T, with angular dependence showing peaks at B//c and B//ab. Statistical validation via t-tests (p<0.05) between samples, ensuring reproducibility across ≥3 replicates. These components reinforce conclusions by isolating variable effects (comparisons/ablations), quantifying improvements (criteria), and ensuring data robustness (statistics), validating that synergistic tuning yields superior pinning.

**Implementation of Technologies/Methods:**

Step 1: Fabrication via Reel-to-Reel MOCVD  
Implement MOCVD on IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tapes (width 12 mm, length up to 10 m) using a continuous deposition system. Precursors (tetramethylheptanedionate complexes of Gd, Yb, Ba, Cu) are vaporized at 250–300°C and delivered via Ar/O2 carrier gas to a heated substrate (750–850°C) at 5–10 Torr. Target film thickness: 0.54 μm. For composition tuning, adjust precursor molar ratios precisely (e.g., Cu/Ba from 1.15–1.21 by varying Cu precursor flow rate 5–10%). Post-deposition oxygenation at 450–500°C in O2 to achieve δ≈0.1. Key aspect: Modular precursor delivery system with mass flow controllers for ratio accuracy (±1%).

Step 2: Microstructure Characterization  
Use cross-sectional TEM (e.g., FEI Tecnai F20 at 200 kV) for imaging nanorods (width, length, density) and nanodots (size, tilt). Prepare samples via focused ion beam milling. Implement 2D-XRD (Bruker D8, Cu Kα, χ=45°) to confirm (011)-BaCuO2 orientation via pole figures. EDS (integrated with TEM) for elemental mapping. For strain, apply geometric phase analysis (GPA) on high-resolution TEM images: GPA processes lattice fringe patterns to map strain fields (ε_xx, ε_yy) with 0.1% resolution, revealing tensile/compressive strains at interfaces. Critical concept: Coherent interfaces are defined as mismatch |f| <6%, verified by absence of dislocations in HRTEM.

Step 3: Performance Measurement  
Four-probe transport Jc: Pattern 50–100 μm wide bridges on tapes, measure Ic at 4–77 K, 0–5 T (B//c and angular 0–180° in 10° steps) using a cryostat with superconducting magnet. Criterion: 1 μV cm⁻¹. Magnetization Jc up to 14 T via PPMS (Quantum Design), applying Bean model: Jc = 20 ΔM / [a(1 - a/3b)], where ΔM is hysteresis loop width, a/b sample dimensions. Calibrate against transport data for accuracy. Angular dependence quantifies bidirectional pinning.

Step 1: Resource and Timeline Evaluation  
Feasible with standard lab equipment: MOCVD system (available commercially pre-2025), TEM/XRD/PPMS (common in materials labs). Timeline: 3 months for sample fabrication (10 samples, 1 week each), 2 months for characterization, 1 month for measurements/analysis. Personnel: 1 PhD student for fabrication, 1 postdoc for TEM/GPA, 1 researcher for Jc tests (total 2–3 people).

Step 2: Potential Challenges and Strategies

### 1. Experimental Design
**Objective:** Optimize the hierarchical pinning architecture in Gd0.5Yb0.5Ba2Cu3O7-δ (GdYbBCO) coated conductors for ultrahigh-field (>20 T) applications by tuning Cu/Ba and (Gd+Yb)/Ba ratios to control self-assembled BaCuO2 nanorods and (Gd,Yb)2O3 nanodots.

**Baselines:**
- **Reference Sample:** Standard GdYBCO (15% Zr-doped) for comparative Jc performance at 4 K, 20 T.
- **Control Samples:** GdYbBCO with fixed RE/Ba=0.65 and Cu/Ba=1.19 (optimal composition) vs. off-ratio samples (Cu/Ba=1.15, 1.21; RE/Ba=0.55, 0.75).

**Comparative Methods:**
- **Microstructure:** Cross-sectional TEM for nanorod/nanodot density, size, and alignment (≥100 nanorods/sample).
- **Strain Analysis:** Geometric phase analysis (GPA) to quantify lattice mismatch and strain fields at interfaces.
- **Transport Properties:** Four-probe Jc measurements (1 μV cm⁻¹ criterion) at 4–77 K, 0–14 T, with angular dependence (0–180°).

**Ablations:**
- **Composition Ablation:** Vary Cu/Ba (1.15–1.21) and RE/Ba (0.55–0.75) to isolate effects on nanorod/nanodot formation.
- **Interface Ablation:** Compare coherent (Cu/Ba=1.19) vs. mismatched (Cu/Ba=1.21) interfaces via TEM dislocation analysis.

**Evaluation Criteria:**
- **Primary:** Jc(4 K, 20 T) > 13 MA cm⁻², α < 0.4, B* > 500 mT.
- **Secondary:** Nanorod aspect ratio (>7:1), nanodot density (>3000 μm⁻²), and strain uniformity (Δε < 2%).

---

### 2. Implementation of Technologies/Methods
**Fabrication:**
1. **Substrate Preparation:** IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tapes (Δω < 2°, Δφ < 4°) cleaned via ultrasonic acetone/methanol.
2. **MOCVD Growth:**
   - Precursors: Gd(TMHD)3, Yb(TMHD)3, Ba(TMHD)2, Cu(TMHD)2.
   - Reel-to-reel deposition at 800°C, 0.5 m/h, 0.54 μm thickness.
   - Precise molar ratios: Cu/Ba (1.15–1.21), RE/Ba (0.55–0.75).
3. **Oxygenation:** Post-anneal at 450°C, 1 atm O2 for 24 h to achieve δ ≈ 0.1.

**Characterization:**
1. **TEM/SEM:** Cross-sectional imaging (FEI Titan, 300 kV) for nanorod/nanodot metrics.
2. **2D-XRD:** PANalytical Empyrean with χ=45° to resolve (011)-BaCuO2 orientation.
3. **EDS:** Compositional mapping (Oxford X-Max 80) to verify stoichiometry.

**Measurements:**
1. **Transport Jc:** Four-probe method (1 μV cm⁻¹ criterion) in PPMS (0–14 T, 4–77 K).
2. **Magnetization Jc:** SQUID-VSM (Quantum Design) up to 14 T, calibrated via Bean model.

---

### 3. Feasibility Assessment
**Equipment/Timelines:**
- **MOCVD System:** Commercial reel-to-reel setup (6 months for optimization).
- **Characterization:** TEM access (1 week/sample), XRD/EDS (2 days/sample).
- **Total Duration:** 12 months (fabrication: 6 months, characterization: 4 months, analysis: 2 months).

**Materials/Risks:**
- **Risks:** Off-ratio compositions may form CuO precipitates (mitigation: in-situ optical monitoring during MOCVD).
- **Mitigation:** Redundant samples (3 tapes per composition) to account for deposition variability.

**References:**
1. *"High-field performance of BaCuO2-nanorod-enhanced REBCO tapes"* (Supercond. Sci. Technol., 2021).
2. *"Strain engineering in MOCVD-grown REBCO coated conductors"* (APL Materials, 2020).

---

### 4. Clarity of Language
- Direct phrasing: "Cu/Ba=1.19 maximizes nanorod density; deviations reduce Jc by 30%."
- Avoid jargon: "Coherent interfaces" → "Interfaces without dislocations."

# Experimental Plan: SEG-123 bulk composition–pinning protocol

## Experimental Draft

### Stage I — Release the comparison design and preparation resources
The objective is to compare BaO₂ suppression of RE/Ba substitution, Ag₂O-assisted liquid-phase modification and their interaction in single-domain SEG-123 bulk grown by top-seeded infiltration growth (TSIG) in air, with Pt fixed. The design uses six BaO₂ levels, 0–5 wt%, and two Ag₂O levels, 0 and 10 wt%, with 0.5 wt% Pt. Three independent growths per cell are proposed (P), giving 36 bulks. Optimize Ba-only compositions within 0–4 wt%; retain 5 wt% as an excess-addition diagnostic. Randomization and matched controls preserve the comparisons.

Use verified SEG-211, additive powders, separate Y-123/Ba₃Cu₅O₈ liquid-source pellets and c-axis-oriented Nd-123 seeds. Required resources include enclosed powder handling, rated pressing equipment, mapped growth and oxygenation furnaces, cutting/polishing equipment, Cu-Kα XRD, FE-SEM/EDS and qualified SQUID capability. A signed process sheet must resolve proposed settings and qualification prerequisites before the comparison batch begins.

### Stage II — Fabricate and oxygenate traceable bulks
Verify incoming phases, weigh and mix additives under the approved mass basis, prepare porous precursor and liquid-source pellets, assemble the seed above the precursor, and execute calibrated TSIG in air with a 0.2 °C h⁻¹ growth window. Oxygenate within 450–350 °C using a qualified schedule, then map and cut matched central/edge specimens.

### Stage III — Characterize, compare and archive
Assess phase assemblage, orthorhombicity, texture, domain consistency and microstructure before interpreting SQUID transition and hysteresis data. Report geometry-normalized magnetic Jc, uncertainty, spatial variation and replicate dispersion. Apply diagnostic gates, preserve failed-parent records and compare against supplied reference targets without claiming attainment. Optional transport remains separately qualified and reported; anticipated outputs are traceable structural, microstructural and magnetic datasets with explicit limitations.

## Detailed Experimental Tasks

### Experimental Task 1: Stage I — Qualify materials, equipment and the randomized composition matrix

#### Specific Content

##### 1. Scope and release prerequisites
Grow single-domain (Sm,Eu,Gd)Ba₂Cu₃O₇−δ by top-seeded infiltration growth (TSIG) in air. Compare BaO₂ suppression of RE/Ba substitution, Ag₂O-assisted liquid-phase modification and their interaction, with Pt fixed. Supplied property values are targets, not measurements generated by this proposal.

**P denotes a proposed setting requiring calibration and approval before production.** Release a signed process sheet resolving precursor composition, additive mass basis, liquid-source quantity, thermal window, seed survival, oxygenation and equipment limits. Do not begin the comparison batch with these unresolved.

SEG-211 means the mixed-RE 211 phase, nominally (Sm,Eu,Gd)₂BaCuO₅, not SEG-123 or Y₂BaCuO₅. The RE ratio is unspecified; use one verified lot throughout. Equimolar Sm:Eu:Gd is a P fallback only after approval.

##### 2. Sample matrix and identifiers

| Factor | Levels | Role |
|---|---|---|
| BaO₂ | 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 wt% | Optimize through 4%; 5% diagnoses excess addition |
| Ag₂O | 0, 10 wt% | Matched no-Ag and Ag arms |
| Pt | 0.5 wt%, all cells | Fixed refiner |
| Replication | P: three independent growths/cell | 36 bulks; not three pieces of one bulk |

Use `SEG-Bxx-Ayy-Rz`, e.g. `SEG-B04-A10-R2`. Append `-M-C`, `-M-E`, `-X`, `-S`, or `-T` for central/edge magnetic, XRD, microscopy or transport specimens. Record parent coordinates and orientation.

Each growth block contains all 12 compositions; randomize preparation order and furnace position. Hold precursor lot, seed geometry, liquid supply, pressing, atmosphere and thermal program constant. B00-A00 is the reference; B00-A10 is Ag-only; Bxx-A00 is Ba-only. Select the optimized Ba level from 0–4 using the Ba-only results before evaluating its matched co-doped arm. The full factorial also estimates interaction without replacing these controls.

##### 3. Materials, equipment and consolidated settings
Use verified SEG-211, BaO₂, Ag₂O, Pt, Y-123, Ba₃Cu₅O₈, c-axis-oriented Nd-123 seeds, compatible crucibles/supports, polishing consumables and nonmagnetic sample holders. Record certificates, actual assays and powder storage history; no unsupported purity requirement is imposed.

Provide a balance, enclosed powder mixer, guarded hydraulic press, mapped air-growth furnace, oxygen-rated annealing furnace with flow monitoring, calibrated thermocouples, diamond saw, polishing equipment, Cu-Kα XRD with texture capability, FE-SEM with BSE/EDS, and SQUID capable of 1 mT, ±5 T and 65–100 K. Verify holder clearance, maximum magnetic moment and field accuracy before cutting coupons.

| Operation | Setting and control |
|---|---|
| Additive weighing | P: mass per dry SEG-211 mass; ±0.1 percentage point for each additive; document balance uncertainty |
| Mixing | P: enclosed dry, low-energy mixing for 4 h; qualify homogeneity and contamination before use |
| Green pellet | P: 10 mm diameter, 200 MPa; thickness/density fixed after infiltration pilot |
| Precursor conditioning | P candidate: 900 °C, 4 h in air; accept only if phase retention and open porosity are demonstrated |
| Liquid source | Y-123 + Ba₃Cu₅O₈; P starting ratio 1:1 molar; source mass and dimensions require pilot calibration |
| TSIG peak | Draft candidate 1050 °C/10 h, not a released setting; calibrate melt formation and seed survival |
| Growth window | 0.2 °C h⁻¹; P rate tolerance ±0.02 °C h⁻¹; calibrated start/end temperatures; P spatial temperature agreement within ±1 °C |
| Oxygenation | 450→350 °C in flowing O₂; P initial duration 72 h, linear descent, then controlled cooling; calibrate flow and oxygen uptake |
| XRD | Cu-Kα; P 2θ = 10–80°, step ≤0.02°; calibrate zero and wavelength |
| FE-SEM | P BSE at 10 kV, 500–10,000×; adjust for phase contrast and charging |
| SQUID | Tc: 1 mT; loops: ±5 T at 65, 77 and P 90 K; H ∥ c within P ±1° |
| Temperature control | P stability ±0.1 K for loops; near Tc use ≤0.2 K steps and equilibrium checks |

The 200 MPa load on a 10 mm die is approximately 15.7 kN; verify press and die ratings. A growth window of ΔT °C takes ΔT/0.2 hours: 20 °C requires 100 h, excluding ramps and holds. Do not confuse cooling rate with a linear crystal-growth velocity.

- The signed release sheet separates proposed settings from approved production conditions. SEG-211 identity and its unspecified RE ratio must remain explicit rather than being replaced by a different precursor or an assumed composition. **Source:** B001, B002.
- The factorial matrix retains no-additive, Ag-only and Ba-only controls with fixed Pt. Selecting the Ba-only optimum within 0–4 wt% before assessing its matched co-doped arm preserves the specified comparison, while 5 wt% remains diagnostic. **Source:** B004, B006.
- The equipment inventory and consolidated settings define qualification needs, not released recipes. Press-load and growth-window calculations support equipment and scheduling checks without interpreting cooling rate as crystal-growth velocity. **Source:** B007, B008, B009, B010.

### Experimental Task 2: Stage II — Prepare pellets, perform TSIG, oxygenate and transfer mapped specimens

#### Specific Content

##### 4. Sequential fabrication and hand-offs
1. **Incoming-material gate.** Obtain powder XRD for SEG-211 and liquid-source constituents; confirm identity and inspect contamination. Hold mislabeled lots. Retain aliquots from every lot.
2. **Weigh and mix.** For precursor mass m, weigh BaO₂ = xm/100, Ag₂O = ym/100 and Pt = 0.005m under the approved basis. Add all refiners before TSIG; do not add Ag after growth. For P m = 10 g, B04-A10 requires 0.40 g BaO₂, 1.00 g Ag₂O and 0.050 g Pt. Independently check calculations and masses. Inspect representative mixed-powder aliquots for segregation.
3. **Condition and press.** Use the qualified conditioning route; gently deagglomerate without unqualified high-energy milling. Press porous precursor pellets and separate liquid-source pellets. Record green mass, dimensions, density and cracks. Do not apply a dense 950 °C/48 h oxygen sinter unless separately shown compatible with infiltration.
4. **Hand-off to growth operator.** Transfer labeled pellets, seed orientation photograph, mass sheet, pilot-approved liquid quantity and thermal recipe. Place liquid source below the SEG-211 body and seed on its upper surface. Qualify crucible compatibility, support geometry and overflow containment; the separate pellets are reagents, not a final layered architecture.
5. **TSIG in air.** Run the approved heat-up, melt/infiltration hold, approach to growth start and 0.2 °C h⁻¹ window. Log actual temperatures continuously. Peak temperature minus growth temperature is not peritectic undercooling; calculate undercooling only from a verified composition-dependent peritectic temperature. Cool after growth at a qualified rate. Photograph growth sectors, seed condition, cracks and leaked liquid.
6. **Hand-off to oxygenation operator.** Transfer parent ID, dimensions, growth log and defect map. Anneal within 450–350 °C using the approved O₂ schedule. Verify uptake/uniformity on pilot coupons; 72 h is not assumed sufficient for every bulk thickness.
7. **Hand-off to characterization.** Map the grown bulk before cutting. Take matched central and edge coupons, excluding the seed and Nd-contaminated region; retain the remainder. P magnetic coupon size is approximately 2 × 1 × 0.5 mm, subject to SQUID qualification. Measure every actual dimension and orientation. Polish adjacent sections to a mirror finish, with P final 0.05 µm alumina; clean gently and avoid unqualified ultrasonication of cracked material.

#### Related Knowledge

- Incoming powder identification, independently checked additive weighing and segregation inspection provide traceable preparation controls. All refiners are introduced before growth, using the approved additive basis. **Source:** B011.
- Separate porous SEG-211 and liquid-source pellets, with the seed above the precursor, define the infiltration assembly. Conditioning, liquid inventory, crucible compatibility and thermal settings remain qualification-dependent; the pellets are reagents rather than a final layered architecture. **Source:** B011.
- Growth, oxygenation and characterization hand-offs carry parent identity, geometry, logs and defect maps. Pilot verification of oxygen uptake and measured coupon geometry prevents assuming that the proposed annealing duration or specimen dimensions are universally suitable. **Source:** B011.

### Experimental Task 3: Stage III — Characterize phase assemblage, texture and inclusion distributions

#### Specific Content

##### 5. Structural and microstructural characterization
Collect powder XRD from a representative fragment and oriented surface scans. Determine phases and lattice parameters with uncertainty; resolve orthorhombic a/b splitting rather than using c alone. Oriented (00l) dominance supports c-axis texture but does not establish phase purity or a single domain. Map several positions with rocking curves and an asymmetric reflection/pole measurement; correlate with sector microscopy and, if ambiguous, orientation mapping.

For c = 11.74 Å, d₀₀₅ = 2.348 Å; Cu-Kα₁ λ ≈1.5406 Å predicts 2θ₀₀₅ ≈38.3°. Confirm indexing against the full pattern. Report c near 11.74 Å without imposing an unsupported acceptance tolerance.

Image equivalent center, intermediate and edge locations. P minimum: five fields/location and at least 100 segmented 211 particles/specimen. Record equivalent-circle diameter distribution, area fraction, clustering, cracks, pores, liquid pools and Ag-rich regions; verify phase assignments by EDS where feasible. Report 3.2–3.3 µm as a supplied comparison, not “sub-micron.” Do not equate area fraction with a stipulated volume fraction or infer atomic RE/Ba occupancy from EDS.

#### Related Knowledge

- Powder and oriented XRD serve different purposes: orthorhombic a/b splitting informs structural assessment, while oriented (00l) dominance alone establishes neither phase purity nor a single domain. Spatial orientation measurements support the domain assessment. **Source:** B012.
- The supplied lattice and reflection calculation supports indexing against the full diffraction pattern. A c parameter near 11.74 Å is reported without inventing an acceptance tolerance. **Source:** B013.
- Equivalent spatial sampling and particle-distribution reporting support microstructural comparisons. The supplied 3.2–3.3 µm comparison is not sub-micron, area fraction is not a stipulated volume fraction, and EDS does not establish atomic RE/Ba occupancy. **Source:** B014.

### Experimental Task 4: Stage III — Measure SQUID transitions and loops and calculate magnetic current density

#### Specific Content

##### 6. SQUID measurements and analysis

# Experimental Plan: SEG-123 bulk composition–pinning protocol

## Experimental Draft

### Stage I — Release the comparison design and preparation resources
The objective is to compare BaO₂ suppression of RE/Ba substitution, Ag₂O-assisted liquid-phase modification and their interaction in single-domain SEG-123 bulk grown by top-seeded infiltration growth (TSIG) in air, with Pt fixed. The design uses six BaO₂ levels, 0–5 wt%, and two Ag₂O levels, 0 and 10 wt%, with 0.5 wt% Pt. Three independent growths per cell are proposed (P), giving 36 bulks. Optimize Ba-only compositions within 0–4 wt%; retain 5 wt% as an excess-addition diagnostic. Randomization and matched controls preserve the comparisons.

Use verified SEG-211, additive powders, separate Y-123/Ba₃Cu₅O₈ liquid-source pellets and c-axis-oriented Nd-123 seeds. Required resources include enclosed powder handling, rated pressing equipment, mapped growth and oxygenation furnaces, cutting/polishing equipment, Cu-Kα XRD, FE-SEM/EDS and qualified SQUID capability. A signed process sheet must resolve proposed settings and qualification prerequisites before the comparison batch begins.

### Stage II — Fabricate and oxygenate traceable bulks
Verify incoming phases, weigh and mix additives under the approved mass basis, prepare porous precursor and liquid-source pellets, assemble the seed above the precursor, and execute calibrated TSIG in air with a 0.2 °C h⁻¹ growth window. Oxygenate within 450–350 °C using a qualified schedule, then map and cut matched central/edge specimens.

### Stage III — Characterize, compare and archive
Assess phase assemblage, orthorhombicity, texture, domain consistency and microstructure before interpreting SQUID transition and hysteresis data. Report geometry-normalized magnetic Jc, uncertainty, spatial variation and replicate dispersion. Apply diagnostic gates, preserve failed-parent records and compare against supplied reference targets without claiming attainment. Optional transport remains separately qualified and reported; anticipated outputs are traceable structural, microstructural and magnetic datasets with explicit limitations.

# Synergistic Optimization Experimental Protocol for Ternary (Sm,Eu,Gd)Ba2Cu3O7−δ Bulk Superconductors

## Research Background and Motivation

In recent years, rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) high-temperature superconductors have attracted considerable attention due to their excellent critical current density (Jc) and relatively high critical temperature (Tc). Particularly, the ternary (Sm,Eu,Gd)Ba2Cu3O7−δ (SEG-123) system can significantly enhance superconducting performance through element-combination optimization ([Akash Garg Agarwal et al., 2025](https://discovery.researcher.life/article/spatial-variations-in-superconducting-and-microstructural-properties-of-bulk-sm-eu-gd-ba2cu3o7--grown-by-top-seeded-infiltration-in-air/4feed3b2a47e324688fac3095c70fcf9)). This research aims to develop a method for low-cost batch preparation of high-performance SEG-123 bulk materials in air through a synergistic doping strategy of BaO2 and Ag2O, meeting the requirements of high-field applications in liquid nitrogen (77 K) and liquid oxygen (90 K) temperature regimes.

Conventional melt-growth (MG) processes suffer from macroscopic porosity, product shrinkage, and inhomogeneous 211 phase distribution, whereas top-seeded infiltration growth (TSIG) technology can effectively overcome these defects ([Miryala Laboratory, 2025](https://miryalalab.com/enhancing-the-superconducting-properties-of-bulk-smeugdba2cu3o7%E2%88%92%CE%B4-impact-of-bao2-and-ag2o-addition-via-infiltration-growth-process-in-air/)). By optimizing the BaO2 content (0-5 wt%), RE/Ba site substitution disorder can be suppressed, while Ag2O (10 wt%) doping can refine 211 particles and introduce additional pinning centers, achieving high-field Jc multiplication without loss of high Tc characteristics.

## Experimental Design and Methods

### Material Preparation

**Precursor Preparation**:
1. Weigh Sm2O3, Eu2O3, Gd2O3, BaCO3, and CuO powders in stoichiometric ratios, ball-mill and mix for 24 hours to prepare SEG-211 ((Sm,Eu,Gd)2BaCuO5) precursor
2. Add different contents of BaO2 (0, 2, 3, 4, 5 wt%) and a fixed amount of Pt (0.5 wt%) as grain refiner
3. Press into cylindrical green bodies with diameter 20 mm and thickness 10 mm

**Infiltration Source Preparation**:
1. Adopt a mixture of Y-123 (YBa2Cu3O7) and Ba3Cu5O8 (3:5) as the liquid-phase infiltration source
2. Add 10 wt% Ag2O to improve melt fluidity and microstructure
3. Press into discs of the same dimensions as the SEG-211 green bodies

**TSIG Growth Process**:
1. Place the SEG-211 green body at the bottom, the infiltration source disc on top, with a Al2O3 spacer in between
2. Induce growth using an Nd-123 seed crystal under air atmosphere, employing a slow heating program:
   - Room temperature to 900°C: 2°C/min
   - 900°C to 1040°C: 1°C/min
   - Hold at 1040°C for 10 hours to promote liquid-phase infiltration
   - Slow cooling (0.2°C/h) through the peritectic reaction temperature window (~1000°C)
3. Perform oxygen-controlled annealing in the 450-350°C temperature range for a total time of 120 hours

### Characterization Techniques

**Structural Characterization**:
1. X-ray diffraction (XRD, Cu-Kα radiation): Analyze phase purity and crystal orientation
2. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM): Observe microstructure and 211 phase distribution
3. Energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS): Determine elemental distribution and stoichiometric ratios

**Superconducting Performance Testing**:
1. Superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) magnetometer:
   - Critical temperature Tc: Measure magnetic susceptibility-temperature curves under 1 mT field
   - Critical current density Jc: Calculate using the extended Bean model from M-H loops (up to 5 T)
2. Transport measurements: Four-probe method to verify macroscopic current-carrying capacity of bulk samples

## Key Optimization Strategies

### Composition Control

**BaO2 Doping Optimization**:
By systematically increasing the BaO2 content (0-5 wt%) in the SEG-211 precursor, a Ba-rich chemical environment is achieved, effectively suppressing RE/Ba antisite defects. Studies show that samples with 4 wt% BaO2 doping exhibit optimal performance:
- Tc(onset) increases from 92.65 K to 94.57 K
- Transition width ΔTc significantly narrows from 3.0 K to 0.88 K (improvement of 71%)
- Self-field Jc (77 K) increases from 25.6 kA/cm² to 33.55 kA/cm² (enhancement of 31%) ([Akash Garg Agarwal et al., 2025](https://discovery.researcher.life/article/spatial-variations-in-superconducting-and-microstructural-properties-of-bulk-sm-eu-gd-ba2cu3o7--grown-by-top-seeded-infiltration-in-air/4feed3b2a47e324688fac3095c70fcf9))

**Ag2O Synergistic Doping**:
Adding 10 wt% Ag2O on the basis of optimized BaO2 (4 wt%) produces dual effects:
1. Forms Ag melt to improve liquid-phase infiltration, promoting homogeneous reaction
2. Releases oxygen to regulate local oxygen partial pressure, forming nanoscale Ag particles as additional pinning centers
Performance enhancements are manifested as:
- High-field Jc (65 K, 3 T) reaches 50.54 kA/cm², which is 4.3 times that of reference samples
- Maintains good superconducting transition characteristics with Tc >93 K and ΔTc <1.5 K

### Microstructure Control

**211 Phase Refinement**:
Through the synergistic action of Pt (0.5 wt%) and Ag2O (10 wt%), the (Sm,Eu,Gd)2BaCuO5 (SEG-211) particle size is controlled to submicron scale (average 3.2-3.3 μm). Refined 211 phase brings the following advantages:

| Parameter | Unoptimized Sample | Optimized Sample | Change Rate |
|------|------------|----------|--------|
| 211 Average Size | 5.8 μm | 3.3 μm | -43% |
| 211/123 Interface Density | 0.28 μm⁻¹ | 0.42 μm⁻¹ | +50% |
| Pinning Force Peak (hmax) | 0.286 | 0.40 | +40% |

Data source: [Miryala Laboratory, 2025](https://miryalalab.com/enhancing-the-superconducting-properties-of-bulk-smeugdba2cu3o7%E2%88%92%CE%B4-impact-of-bao2-and-ag2o-addition-via-infiltration-growth-process-in-air/)

**Single-Domain Growth Control**:
Using c-axis oriented Nd-123 seed crystal and a slow growth rate of 0.2°C/h ensures single-domain epitaxial growth along the [001] direction. XRD analysis shows only (00l) diffraction peaks with no spurious phases from spontaneous nucleation, ensuring low-angle grain boundaries and high intergranular Jc.

## Feasibility Analysis and Risk Assessment

### Equipment and Material Requirements

**Core Equipment List**:
1. High-temperature box furnace (maximum 1200°C, temperature control accuracy ±1°C)
2. Ball mill (rotation speed 200-400 rpm)
3. Press (10-20 tons)
4. X-ray diffractometer (Cu-Kα source)
5. Field-emission scanning electron microscope (resolution <5 nm)
6. SQUID magnetometer (magnetic field range 0-5 T)

- Rare-earth oxides (Sm2O3, Eu2O3, Gd2O3): account for ~45% of total cost

| 5 | Data analysis and paper writing | 6 weeks | Complete research report |

### Risks and Countermeasures

**Key Risks and Solutions**:

1. **Difficulty in fully suppressing RE/Ba substitution**:
   - Risk: Even with the addition of BaO2, RE/Ba substitution may still occur at high growth temperatures
   - Solution: Strictly control the temperature window (1000±5°C) and oxygen partial pressure (air flow rate 0.5 L/min)

2. **Non-uniform Ag distribution**:
   - Risk: Ag2O may locally agglomerate to form large particles at high temperatures
   - Solution: Optimize the heating program, pre-sinter at 800°C for 2 hours to promote uniform Ag distribution

3. **Single-domain growth failure**:
   - Risk: Spontaneous nucleation leads to polycrystalline formation
   - Solution: Use high-quality Nd-123 seed crystal, ensure surface cleanliness and flatness (<1 μm roughness)

   - Operating temperature can cover liquid nitrogen (77 K) and liquid oxygen (90 K) temperature ranges

This study proposes a systematic approach to optimize SEG-123 bulk superconductors through synergistic doping with BaO2 and Ag2O. The experimental design covers the entire process from material preparation, structural characterization to performance testing, focusing on resolving key scientific issues such as suppression of RE/Ba substitution and optimization of pinning centers. The TSIG air growth process not only reduces production costs, but also lays the foundation for industrial-scale batch preparation.

A. Objectives and Hypotheses
- Objective: Develop a cost-effective TSIG route in air to produce single-domain SEG-123 bulks with high Tc (>93 K) and significantly enhanced high-field Jc by combining (i) BaO2-driven Ba-rich chemistry to suppress RE/Ba anti-site disorder and sharpen Tc, (ii) Ag2O-assisted liquid-phase engineering to generate additional field-induced pinning, and (iii) Pt-assisted refinement of 211 particles to increase 211/123 interface density.
- Hypotheses:
  1) Moderate BaO2 addition to the SEG-211 precursor raises the local Ba chemical potential during infiltration, suppressing RE/Ba substitution, sharpening the superconducting transition (smaller ΔTc) and strengthening δTc-type pinning.
  2) Co-doping with 10 wt% Ag2O provides transient oxygen and dispersed Ag nanoparticles, refining 211 and generating additional pinning centers without degrading Tc.
  3) A separate Ba–Cu–O liquid-source pellet (Y-123 + Ba3Cu5O8) and porous SEG-211 preform avoid liquid pools, macro-segregation, and enable uniform 211 distribution.

D. Implementation of Technologies/Methods
D1. Powder synthesis and preform fabrication
- SEG-211 powder synthesis:
  • Weigh high-purity (≥99.9%) Sm2O3, Eu2O3, Gd2O3, BaCO3, CuO to RE:Ba:Cu = 2:1:1 (RE-211 stoichiometry) with chosen RE ratios.  
  • Ball-mill in isopropanol with 0.5 wt% PVB binder and zirconia media for 12 h; dry at 80 °C.  
  • Calcine at 900 °C (in air) for 12 h; regrind; second calcination at 950 °C for 12 h; confirm phase by XRD (RE-211).  
- Additives blending:
  • Incorporate BaO2 (as designed), Pt powder (0 or 0.5 wt%), and Ag2O (only for Series 3) to the 211 powder in anhydrous IPA; gentle milling 2 h to avoid BaO2 decomposition. Dry below 80 °C under N2.  
  • Safety: Handle BaO2/Ag2O in dry room; avoid contact with organics and moisture; store in desiccator.
- Preform pressing and presinter:
  • Press into Ø12 mm × 6 mm green bodies at 150–200 MPa uniaxial, followed by cold isostatic pressing at 250 MPa.  
  • Presinter in air at 920–940 °C for 4 h to bond particles while retaining 30–35% open porosity for infiltration; measure apparent porosity by Archimedes method; target 0.25–0.35 open porosity.

D2. Liquid-source pellet
- Composition design:
  • Use a Y-123 + Ba3Cu5O8 mix (or BaCuO2 + CuO) to form a Ba–Cu–O liquid slightly Ba-rich at 1020–1040 °C. A practical mixture is BaCuO2:CuO ≈ 65:35 mol% plus ~10 vol% Y-123 powder to modulate wetting and viscosity.  
  • Press into Ø12 mm × 2 mm pellet; presinter at 880 °C for 2 h for mechanical integrity (avoid full melting).
- Rationale: The Ba–Cu–O liquid forms above ~1000 °C and infiltrates the porous 211 compact. A slight Ba-rich liquid mitigates RE/Ba intersite substitution in the growing 123 phase.

D3. Top-seeded infiltration growth (TSIG) in air
- Stack architecture (top to bottom): Nd-123 seed on MgO buffer tab (optional) on SEG-211 preform; separate liquid-source pellet under the preform; all on dense Al2O3 setter.  
- Thermal profile (air, programmable box or vertical furnace with gradient <3 K across sample):
  1) Ramp 100 °C/h to 500 °C, dwell 2 h to remove residual binders and decompose Ag2O (to Ag + O2) safely.  
  2) Ramp 150 °C/h to 1035–1045 °C, dwell 60–90 min to fully form Ba–Cu–O liquid in the source pellet.  
  3) Lower to growth window 1005–1015 °C (just below the effective peritectic of SEG-123), then slow cool at 0.2 °C/h to 980 °C to promote seeded epitaxial growth and controlled infiltration/consumption of 211.  
  4) Furnace cool to 500 °C at 60 °C/h; then to room temperature.
- Notes:
  • Use an alumina catch tray to avoid melt run-out.  
  • The slow 0.2 °C/h segment defines the single-domain growth front; verify no spontaneous nucleation around the seed.

D4. Oxygenation
- Post-anneal in flowing O2:
  • Ramp to 450 °C at 60 °C/h; dwell 150–200 h; slow cool to 350 °C at 10 °C/h; dwell 50–100 h; slow cool to room temperature.  
  • Purpose: Achieve orthorhombic, oxygenated 123 with c ≈ 11.74 Å and narrow ΔTc.

D5. Structural, microstructural and compositional characterization
- X-ray diffraction (Cu Kα): θ–2θ from 10–80°, step 0.02°.  
  • Confirm phase purity (123 dominant, minor 211), orthorhombicity (peak splitting), and c-axis texture (only 00l peaks for top face).  
  • Optional: Rietveld refinement with constrained occupancies to estimate RE/Ba anti-site level trends across BaO2 series.  
- FE-SEM (backscattered/electron secondary imaging) + EDS/WDS:
  • Map and quantify 211 particle size (target mean 3–4 µm) and distribution using image analysis on multiple fields; measure area fraction of 211; detect Ag nanoparticles, Pt-rich inclusions, and any residual liquid pools.  
  • Radial uniformity: sections at center and edge; quantify porosity and inclusion density.  
- Iodometric titration or TGA-O2 to benchmark oxygen content δ for selected samples; cross-check with c-axis lattice parameter.

D6. Superconducting and electromagnetic measurements
- SQUID magnetometry:
  • M–T at 1 mT after zero-field cooling (ZFC) from 120 K to 10 K; Tc(onset) and ΔTc (10–90% criterion).  
  • M–H loops at 65, 77, 90 K up to 5 T (±H max), sweeping slowly (≤10 mT/s) to minimize heating.  
  • Jc from extended Bean model for rectangular prisms: Jc = 20 ΔM/[a(1 − a/3b)] with a ≤ b (a,b in cm; ΔM in emu cm−3). Evaluate demagnetization corrections by geometry.  
  • Determine irreversibility field Hirr(T) by Kramer extrapolation; plot Fp = Jc μ0 H vs reduced field h = H/Hirr; extract hmax and compare to Dew-Hughes models (δl typically hmax ≈ 0.2; δTc/normal-core ≈ 0.33–0.4).  
- Four-probe resistivity (optional cross-check): ρ–T at 10 mA current density; confirm ΔTc and Tc.  
- Trapped field (application proxy): Field-cool in 1.5–2 T at 77 K; remove field; scan trapped field with Hall probe above center and across radius; compare between baseline and optimized samples.

E. Data Analysis and Result Evaluation Criteria
- Reliability and statistics:
  • Use n ≥ 3 per composition; report mean ± SD; use one-way ANOVA with Tukey post-hoc for multiple comparisons of Jc(77 K, 0 T), Jc(65 K, 3 T), Tc, ΔTc, mean 211 size.  
  • Success criterion for BaO2 effect: statistically significant ΔTc narrowing and Tc increase over baseline without Jc degradation in self-field.  
  • Success criterion for Ag2O co-doping: statistically significant enhancement of high-field Jc (e.g., ≥2× at 65–77 K, H ≥ 2–3 T) with Tc > 93 K and ΔTc < 1.5 K.  
  • Microstructural correlation: Jc improvements must correlate with refined 211 size distribution, increased 211/123 interface area, and absence of liquid inclusions.  
  • Pinning mechanism: hmax shift toward 0.33–0.4 indicates δTc-type pinning; fit Fp(h) to Dew-Hughes scalings and compare residuals.

F. Feasibility, Resources, and Risk Mitigation
- Equipment: High-T furnace with precise control and low gradients; oxygen annealing tube furnace; SEM/EDS; XRD; SQUID magnetometer up to 5 T; Hall probe and magnet for trapped field. All are standard in condensed matter/materials labs.
- Materials: Commercial RE oxides, BaCO3, CuO, BaO2, Ag2O, Pt powder, Nd-123 seeds (commercial or previously grown), Ba–Cu–O precursors.
- Timeline (single iteration): Powder/calcinations (1 week), preforms and liquid-source pellets (2 days), TSIG run (3–4 days including slow cool), oxygenation (1–2 weeks), characterization and analysis (2 weeks). Full matrix with ablations: ~3–4 months.
- Potential challenges and mitigations:
  • Excess BaO2 (>4–5 wt%) may cause liquid pools/inclusions: constrain to ≤4 wt% for mainline, and rely on separate liquid-source and controlled porosity to homogenize infiltration.  
  • Ag2O decomposition gas release: stage a slow dwell at 400–500 °C to safely decompose; ensure venting.  
  • RE/Ba substitution quantification is subtle: complement Rietveld with EDS line scans and Tc/ΔTc trends; consider STEM-EDS on selected samples if available.  
  • Seed dissolution: use MgO buffer and limit peak T duration; ensure stable seed placement.  
  • Porosity control: verify open porosity after presinter; if too low, reduce presinter T by 10–20 °C.

G. Comparative and Ablation Study Details
- BaO2-only series (0–5 wt%): Quantify Tc, ΔTc, Jc(77 K, 0–1 T) and Jc(65 K, 3–5 T), Fp(h), hmax; SEM quantify 211 size; XRD orthorhombicity and c parameter; choose optimum BaO2 at maximum Jc(77 K) and minimum ΔTc with no inclusions.
- Ag2O co-doping at optimum BaO2: Repeat full measurements; expect larger high-field Jc gains; verify Tc remains high and ΔTc narrow; correlate with finer 211 and Ag nano-inclusions.
- Pt ablation (0 vs 0.5 wt%): Compare 211 size, Jc(H), Fp(h) to validate Pt role in refinement and δTc pinning.
- Liquid-source architecture: Separate vs mixed; target fewer residual liquid inclusions and more uniform 211 distribution in the separate approach; compare radial uniformity of Jc and ΔTc.
- Growth window/seed: Faster cool (0.5 °C/h) and MgO seed expected to increase secondary nucleation and misorientation; quantify via XRD texture and inter-grain Jc drop; retain 0.2 °C/h and Nd-123 seed as the optimized condition.

H. Measurement Parameters and Acceptance Windows
- Jc extraction: Use sample dimensions measured to ±5 µm; correct for demagnetizing factor for thin disks; verify Bean-model consistency by varying H sweep rate.  
- Temperature calibration: Platinum RTD near sample; verify 77 K and 65 K with LN2 and controlled cryostat.  
- XRD texture: Require only 00l peaks above background within ±5° of normal for top face; rocking curve FWHM < 3–5° preferred.  
- Microstructure target: Mean 211 particle size 2–4 µm with narrow distribution; no visible >10 µm liquid pockets in polished cross-sections.

I. Expected Outcomes and Decision Points
- If BaO2 ≤4 wt% narrows ΔTc and raises Tc without inclusions, fix this as the composition baseline.  
- If Ag2O 10 wt% increases Jc at high fields while keeping Tc > 93 K and ΔTc < 1.5 K, select as the production-grade dopant set.  
- If Pt 0.5 wt% materially refines 211 and raises Jc relative to 0 wt% Pt, retain Pt.  
- If mixed-pellet architecture shows macro-segregation, mandate separate liquid-source pellets for batch production.

K. Notes on Critical Concepts (plain language)
- TSIG: A porous 211 “sponge” is infiltrated by a Ba–Cu–O liquid that reacts to form the 123 superconducting phase. Separating the liquid-source pellet from the 211 preform helps control the amount and distribution of liquid, preventing defects.  
- RE/Ba anti-site disorder: Rare-earth ions on the Ba sites distort the lattice and depress Tc, making the transition broader. A Ba-rich liquid during growth reduces this undesired substitution.  
- δl vs δTc pinning: δl (mean-free-path) pinning arises from weak nanoscale disorder; δTc (order parameter) pinning arises from stronger inhomogeneities such as 211/123 interfaces or normal inclusions, generally giving a higher hmax (~0.33–0.4).  
- Ag2O: Decomposes to Ag and O2 at moderate temperatures; Ag metal disperses and can form nanoscale inclusions and alter wetting of the liquid, while released oxygen assists oxygenation, jointly increasing pinning and connectivity.  
- Pt: Acts as a heterogeneous nucleation catalyst for 211 particles, keeping them small and well-dispersed, which increases the number of effective pinning centers.

Step 9: Conduct trapped-field tests at 77 K as an application proxy.
