Title: Thickness-driven pinning landscape engineering in 3.3 µm EuBa2Cu3O7−δ with 6 mol% BaHfO3 for ultra-high Jc at 4.2 K and reduced angular anisotropy

Objective and Hypotheses
- Objective: Develop and validate an industrially scalable process that exploits thickness-dependent microstructure evolution in EuBa2Cu3O7−δ (EuBCO) doped with 6 mol% BaHfO3 (BHO) to create a three-dimensional (3-D) mixed pinning landscape combining highly splayed BHO nanocolumns/nanoparticles, tolerated low-angle grain boundaries, and controlled interface quality, to achieve:
  - Jc ≈ 5 MA/cm² at 4.2 K, 14 T (B parallel to c-axis) in 3.3 µm films.
  - Angular anisotropy ratio < 1.2 at 30 K, 5 T.
  - Tc ≈ 97 K with narrow transition ΔTc ≈ 0.6 K.
- Hypotheses:
  1) High-rate, multi-cycle MPMT-PLD with dynamic temperature control increases BHO nanocolumn splay (0–20°) and produces a dense mix of correlated and random pins, slowing Jc(B) decay and reducing Jc(θ) anisotropy.
  2) Accepting limited misoriented EuBCO grains nucleated on Cu–O particles introduces additional isotropic pinning without severely suppressing Tc, causing a modest reduction in self-field Jc at 77 K but improved in-field performance.
  3) A step-wise heater-temperature ramp during multi-cycle deposition preserves an optimal growth window at the bottom interface, maintaining c-axis template quality and high Tc in thick films.
  4) Intermittent thermal cycling partially relaxes growth stress, limiting microstrain increase and preventing cracking.

Experimental Design
- Overview: A factorial study on IBAD-textured templates compares baseline and modified processes to isolate the roles of (i) BHO content and morphology, (ii) misoriented grains, (iii) interface control via temperature ramp, (iv) thickness/multi-cycle stress management.

A. Sample Matrix and Controls
- Substrates and buffers: Hastelloy tape with standard buffer stack (e.g., Y2O3/YSZ/CeO2 or LaMnO3) on IBAD-MgO templates with in-plane Δφ ≈ 4–6° and out-of-plane Δω ≈ 3–5°. Tape width: 4–10 mm. Use 20–50 cm segments for development.
- Target compositions: 
  - EuBCO (stoichiometric, 1–2% excess Cu to reduce cation deficiency).
  - EuBCO + 6 mol% BHO (single composite target for production runs); optional auxiliary pure BHO target for fine adjustment in multi-plume mode.
- Sample sets (n ≥ 3 per condition for statistics):
  1) Baseline thin control: EuBCO + 6% BHO, 1.1 µm, single-cycle deposition, standard temperature (constant heater setpoint), minimal splay (benchmark).
  2) Baseline thick control: EuBCO + 6% BHO, 3.3 µm, single-cycle (no thermal breaks, no ramp), standard temperature (tests stress and texture limits).
  3) Target process: EuBCO + 6% BHO, 3.3 µm, multi-cycle (6 sub-layers ~0.55 µm each) with step-wise heater-temperature ramp and rotation/speed schedule designed to increase splay.
  4) Ablations:
     - A1 (no BHO): EuBCO, 3.3 µm, multi-cycle ramp (tests BHO necessity).
     - A2 (no ramp): EuBCO + 6% BHO, 3.3 µm, multi-cycle without heater ramp (tests interface control).
     - A3 (low splay): EuBCO + 6% BHO, 3.3 µm, multi-cycle with reduced growth rate and plume symmetry (tests splay role).
     - A4 (suppress misorientation): EuBCO + 6% BHO, 3.3 µm, process tuned to minimize Cu–O particles (tests misoriented-grain contribution).
     - A5 (single-cycle stress): EuBCO + 6% BHO, 3.3 µm, single cycle with same net fluence (tests stress relaxation).

B. Deposition Protocol (MPMT-PLD)
- System: Industrial multi-plume, multi-turn PLD (MPMT-PLD) with reel-to-reel handling; KrF excimer laser (248 nm).
- Laser and plume parameters:
  - Repetition rate: 300 Hz (per active plume); 2–4 synchronized plumes for uniform coverage.
  - Pulse energy: 700–1000 mJ; spot area 20–40 mm²; fluence 1.5–2.5 J/cm².
  - Plume-to-substrate distance: 45–60 mm; plume incidence angle adjusted to distribute particulates.
- Ambient: O2 pressure 0.8–1.0 Torr during growth; 200–400 Torr during post-growth cool-down; ex situ oxygenation as detailed below.
- Temperature control:
  - Heater setpoint 1000–1100 °C (to maintain tape surface ~780–820 °C; confirm by two-color pyrometry and embedded thermocouple calibration).
  - Multi-cycle temperature ramp: For 6 cycles to 3.3 µm, ramp heater +15–25 °C per cycle relative to previous cycle’s setpoint to compensate for view-factor and surface-cooling changes as topography evolves; adjust tape speed to maintain constant surface temperature within ±5 °C of the target growth window.
- Tape speed and rate:
  - Stationary or step-and-repeat during development; for continuous runs, linear speed 0.2–0.5 m/h equivalent to a net deposition rate 0.8–1.5 nm/s per plume, yielding ~0.55 µm per cycle in 6–12 min of net ablation.
  - Between cycles: 3–5 min dwell at growth ambient for thermal equilibration; optional short 1 min oxygen burst to 2 Torr to smooth the surface.
- Splay control:
  - Increase splay by: higher instantaneous growth rate (300 Hz, multi-plume), slight oscillations of oxygen pressure (±0.1–0.2 Torr) at cycle transitions, programmed variation of substrate rotation speed (e.g., 5–15 rpm modulation) and minor off-axis plume alignment (±5–10°) to promote meandering; reduce splay in A3 by lowering rate (≤100 Hz) and enforcing axial plume symmetry.
- Particulate/misoriented grain tuning:
  - To tolerate controlled misorientation (target condition): slightly Cu-rich target (1–2%) and brief low pO2 pre-burst (0.6 Torr for 30 s) at cycle start to allow sparse Cu–O nanoparticle nucleation that seeds isolated a-axis grains; suppress in A4 by using stoichiometric target and maintaining pO2 ≥1 Torr at cycle start with higher surface temperature for enhanced 2D layer-by-layer growth.
- Post-growth oxygenation:
  - Cool in 400 Torr O2 from growth temperature to 500 °C at 10 °C/min; ex situ anneal in flowing O2 (1 bar) at 450 °C for 60–90 min; cool to room temperature in O2 to set δ for Tc ≈ 97 K.

C. Structural and Microstructural Characterization
- X-ray diffraction (high-resolution):
  - θ–2θ scans: confirm c-axis orientation, extract c-axis lattice parameter using Nelson–Riley extrapolation (target ≈ 11.73 Å).
  - Rocking curve (ω-scan) of (005): FWHM target ≈ 1.5° across thickness.
  - φ-scan of (103): FWHM target ≈ 2°; evaluate texture uniformity at multiple positions along length.
  - Williamson–Hall plots: estimate microstrain; target increase from ~0.21% (1.1 µm) to ≤0.25% (3.3 µm).
- SEM and AFM:
  - Surface roughness per cycle (Rq target ≤ 5–8 nm); detect particulates.
- Cross-sectional TEM/STEM:
  - Lamellae at 0.3, 1.1, 2.2, 3.3 µm depths via FIB; HAADF-STEM imaging for BHO nanocolumns and nanoparticles; quantify:
    - Column diameter (3–8 nm), density (vol% 4–10%), spacing (10–20 nm), and length continuity.
    - Splay angle distribution: mean and FWHM per depth; goal: broadened 0–20° distribution in thick film vs narrow near-0° in thin control.
    - Fraction of a-axis grains and low-angle boundaries; correlate with Cu–O particle density via EDS (Hf-M, Ba-L, Eu-M, Cu-K mapping).
  - STEM-EELS/EDS: confirm Hf-rich nanocolumn composition (Ba:Hf ≈ 1:1), verify BHO-free layered regions and their thickness/spacing.
- Residual stress and integrity:
  - Cross-sectional SEM/TEM to check for cracks/voids; bend tests to 1% tensile strain to verify no catastrophic cracking.

D. Electrical and Magnetic Measurements
- Resistivity and Tc:
  - Four-probe ρ(T) in PPMS: 300–10 K at 1–5 mA; Tc onset and ΔTc (10–90% criterion); goal Tc ≈ 97 K, ΔTc ≈ 0.6 K.
- Self-field Jc at 77 K:
  - Transport on 3–5 mm wide bridges; 1 µV/cm criterion; compare targeted process vs A4 (suppressed misorientation). Accept modest reduction (e.g., 1.4 vs 2.6 MA/cm²).
- In-field magnetization Jc:
  - PPMS VSM/Magnet up to 16–18 T, 4.2 K and 30 K; extract Jc using Bean model for rectangular cross-section; measure Fp = JcB.
  - Determine Birr via Kramer plots (Jc^1/2 vs B).
- Angular transport Jc:
  - 18 T split-pair or resistive magnet with rotator; 4.2 K and 30 K; 1 µV/cm criterion; θ sweep 0–180° at fixed B: 5, 10, 14, 18 T; alignment accuracy ±0.2°; compute anisotropy ratio Γ = Jc,max/Jc,min; target Γ < 1.2 at 30 K, 5 T; measure peak broadening near H||c.

E. Data Analysis and Evaluation Criteria
- Pinning-force scaling:
  - Fit reduced field b = B/Birr; Dew-Hughes model Fp(b) ~ b^p(1−b)^q; track bmax shift (random pins bmax ≈ 0.2–0.3; correlated pins shifts and shoulder formation).
  - Compare Fp,max and Fp at 14–18 T to quantify high-field improvements.
- Anisotropic scaling:
  - Apply Blatter scaling with mass anisotropy γ (expected ~5–7 for REBCO). Quantify deviations from scaling as a measure of correlated pin dominance and splay effectiveness.
- Thickness effects:
  - Plot Jc and Fp vs thickness for 1.1, 2.2, 3.3 µm; ensure slower Jc(B) decay at 4.2 K and improved Jc(θ) isotropy with thickness in target process vs controls.
- Texture-performance linkage:
  - Correlate ω, φ FWHM and fraction of a-axis grains with self-field and in-field Jc; verify low-angle boundaries do not depress Tc or broaden ΔTc.
- Success criteria:
  - Achieve Jc ≈ 5 MA/cm² at 4.2 K, 14 T (H||c) on 3.3 µm films with Γ < 1.2 at 30 K, 5 T, Tc ≈ 97 K, ΔTc ≤ 0.6 K, ω ≈ 1.5°, φ ≈ 2°.

Ablation Study Design (Isolate Each Strategy)
- Remove BHO (A1): Expect strong drop in high-field Jc and restoration of stronger anisotropy; confirms necessity of nanocolumn/nanoparticle pins.
- Remove ramp (A2): Expect degraded Tc and broader ΔTc due to interface degradation; possible increased a-axis grains at bottom; confirms interface-temperature control.
- Reduce splay (A3): Expect pronounced c-axis peak in Jc(θ) and higher anisotropy; Fp(b) peak shifts toward lower b; confirms splay role in isotropy.
- Suppress misorientation (A4): Expect higher 77 K self-field Jc but lower high-field Jc and increased anisotropy; confirms beneficial isotropic pin contribution from tolerated misorientation.
- Single-cycle growth (A5): Expect higher microstrain (≥0.28%), possible crack initiation and slightly worse texture; confirms stress-relief role of multi-cycle deposition.

Implementation of Technologies and Methods
- MPMT-PLD Hardware and Process Control
  - Multi-plume optics: Beam splitters or multiple lasers addressing composite EuBCO+BHO targets; synchronized scanning to obtain uniform ablation and stoichiometry.
  - Temperature metrology: Two-color pyrometer aimed at tape surface; embedded thermocouple in dummy substrate for absolute calibration; closed-loop control to achieve ±5 °C stability.
  - Oxygen delivery: Fast-acting MFCs and throttling valve to program ±0.1–0.2 Torr excursions at cycle boundaries.
  - Substrate motion: Programmable rotation 5–30 rpm with sinusoidal modulation; reel-to-reel motion with pause points for cycle transitions.
  - Target management: Densified ceramic EuBCO+BHO target (>95% theoretical density) sintered 950–1000 °C; raster scanning to minimize cone formation; target conditioning 10–15 min prior to deposition.
- Growth Window Rationale
  - REBCO PLD optimal surface temperature is ~770–820 °C; industrial heater setpoints near 1000–1100 °C compensate for radiative losses and emissivity of moving tapes. The multi-cycle ramp compensates for increased radiative loss and morphology-induced view-factor changes as thickness accumulates.
- BHO Nanocolumn Formation and Splay
  - Self-assembly of perovskite BHO nanocolumns occurs by strain-driven phase separation during PLD; higher growth rate and mild off-axis plume incidence promote meandering and splay. Nanoparticle co-precipitates form when local supersaturation and growth interruptions occur at cycle boundaries, adding random point/short-range pins.
- Managing Misoriented Grains
  - Sparse Cu–O nanoparticles (few per µm²) can seed locally misoriented EuBCO grains with low-angle boundaries. By slightly Cu-rich targets and brief low pO2 at cycle begins, their density can be tuned. Boundaries act as isotropic pins when angle is small; excessive density is avoided to prevent weak-link networks.
- Interface Preservation
  - First sub-layer deposited with carefully maintained surface temperature and slightly higher pO2 to maximize epitaxy from buffer template. Subsequent layers use dynamic adjustments to preserve c-axis dominance while allowing controlled splay.
- Oxygenation Protocol
  - Thick films require thorough oxygenation; staged cool-down and ex situ anneal ensure δ optimized for high Tc while avoiding Hf oxide reduction or secondary reactions.

Feasibility Assessment
- Equipment and Resources
  - Industrial MPMT-PLD line (KrF lasers, multi-plume heads), oxygen delivery, reel-to-reel handling, XRD with rocking/phi capability, FIB and TEM/STEM with EDS/EELS, PPMS with VSM and rotator, 18 T transport magnet station, cryogenic infrastructure.
  - Materials: IBAD templates, EuBCO and BHO powders, composite targets, oxygen supply.
  - Personnel: 1 PLD process engineer, 1 materials scientist (XRD/SEM/AFM), 1 TEM specialist, 1 low-temperature transport specialist, 1 data analyst.
- Timeline (indicative)
  - Months 0–1: Target fabrication and PLD calibration (rate/temperature mapping, pyrometry).
  - Months 2–3: Make sample sets (baseline and target), initial XRD/SEM, 77 K self-field measurements.
  - Months 3–5: TEM/STEM across thickness; PPMS magnetization, 18 T transport angular studies.
  - Month 6: Ablation sets (A1–A5), analysis, model fitting, iteration if needed.
- Risks and Mitigations
  - Excess particulates or high a-axis fraction: Mitigate via plume conditioning, target resurfacing, higher pO2 at cycle start, and optimized rotation.
  - Delamination/cracking in thick films: Use multi-cycle stress relief, verify microstrain by Williamson–Hall; adjust cycle thickness if needed.
  - Oxygen deficiency in thick films: Extend ex situ anneal or add in situ high-pO2 soak; verify by Tc and ρ(T) residual resistivity ratio.
  - Hf segregation or secondary phases: Maintain growth window; verify via EDS line scans and adjust growth rate or pO2 to keep BHO coherent.
  - Reproducibility along length: Sample at leading/middle/trailing tape sections; ensure ±10% uniformity in Jc and texture metrics.

Clarity Notes (key terms)
- c-axis and a-axis grains: EuBCO has layered crystal structure; c-axis perpendicular to tape; a-axis grains are misoriented and can create weaker links if excessive.
- Splayed nanocolumns: Columnar BHO defects tilted at various angles; they act as correlated pinning sites and broaden the angular range of strong pinning.
- Bean model: Converts magnetic hysteresis into Jc by assuming a critical state current distribution.
- Dew-Hughes scaling: Empirical model to categorize dominant pinning mechanisms from Fp(b) behavior.
- Anisotropic scaling (Blatter): Rescales field by effective mass anisotropy to test whether pinning is dominated by random, uncorrelated defects; deviations indicate correlated pinning.

Step-by-Step Summary
Step 1: Calibrate MPMT-PLD growth window (surface temperature vs heater setpoint; deposition rate vs laser parameters; oxygen transients).
Step 2: Fabricate baseline 1.1 µm and 3.3 µm films (single-cycle and multi-cycle), plus ablation sets A1–A5.
Step 3: Execute multi-cycle process with per-cycle heater ramp and programmed splay-promoting parameters (rate, rotation, pO2 modulation).
Step 4: Oxygenate and cool using staged protocol; dice test bridges.
Step 5: Perform XRD (θ–2θ, ω, φ), extract c-axis (Nelson–Riley), microstrain (Williamson–Hall).
Step 6: TEM/STEM-EDS across thickness to quantify nanocolumn density, splay distribution, nanoparticle population, a-axis fraction, Cu–O seeds.
Step 7: Measure ρ(T), Tc, and ΔTc; 77 K self-field Jc; PPMS magnetization Jc(B) at 4.2 K and 30 K; extract Fp(b), Birr.
Step 8: Transport Jc(θ) at 4.2 K and 30 K in 5–18 T; compute anisotropy ratio and compare with Blatter scaling predictions.
Step 9: Analyze ablation results to attribute performance gains to BHO content/morphology, splay, interface control, and misorientation; confirm stress relief via microstrain and integrity checks.
Step 10: Iterate process parameters if needed to meet targets; document process windows compatible with meter-scale production.

Criteria for Validation
- Structural: ω ≤ 1.6°, φ ≤ 2.2°, c ≈ 11.73 Å stable; microstrain ≤ 0.25% at 3.3 µm; absence of cracks.
- Electrical: Tc ≈ 97 K, ΔTc ≤ 0.6 K; Jc(4.2 K, 14 T, H||c) ≈ 5 MA/cm²; Γ(30 K, 5 T) < 1.2.
- Causality: Ablation studies show expected directional changes in Jc(B,θ), Fp(b), and Tc/ΔTc, confirming each strategy’s role.

  - PPMS VSM/Magnet up to 16–18 T, 4.2 K and 30 K; extract Jc using Bean model for rectangular cross-section; measure Fp = JcB.

- Angular transport Jc:
  - 18 T split-pair or resistive magnet with rotator; 4.2 K and 30 K; 1 µV/cm criterion; θ sweep 0–180° at fixed B: 5, 10, 14, 18 T; alignment accuracy ±0.2°; compute anisotropy ratio Γ = Jc,max/Jc,min; target Γ < 1.2 at 30 K, 5 T; measure peak broadening near H||c.

E. Data Analysis and Evaluation Criteria
- Pinning-force scaling:
  - Fit reduced field b = B/Birr; Dew-Hughes model Fp(b) ~ b^p(1−b)^q; track bmax shift (random pins bmax ≈ 0.2–0.3; correlated pins shifts and shoulder formation).
  - Compare Fp,max and Fp at 14–18 T to quantify high-field improvements.
- Anisotropic scaling:
  - Apply Blatter scaling with mass anisotropy γ (expected ~5–7 for REBCO). Quantify deviations from scaling as a measure of correlated pin dominance and splay effectiveness.
- Thickness effects:
  - Plot Jc and Fp vs thickness for 1.1, 2.2, 3.3 µm; ensure slower Jc(B) decay at 4.2 K and improved Jc(θ) isotropy with thickness in target process vs controls.
- Texture-performance linkage:
  - Correlate ω, φ FWHM and fraction of a-axis grains with self-field and in-field Jc; verify low-angle boundaries do not depress Tc or broaden ΔTc.
- Success criteria:
  - Achieve Jc ≈ 5 MA/cm² at 4.2 K, 14 T (H||c) on 3.3 µm films with Γ < 1.2 at 30 K, 5 T, Tc ≈ 97 K, ΔTc ≤ 0.6 K, ω ≈ 1.5°, φ ≈ 2°.

Ablation Study Design (Isolate Each Strategy)
- Remove BHO (A1): Expect strong drop in high-field Jc and restoration of stronger anisotropy; confirms necessity of nanocolumn/nanoparticle pins.
- Remove ramp (A2): Expect degraded Tc and broader ΔTc due to interface degradation; possible increased a-axis grains at bottom; confirms interface-temperature control.
- Reduce splay (A3): Expect pronounced c-axis peak in Jc(θ) and higher anisotropy; Fp(b) peak shifts toward lower b; confirms splay role in isotropy.
- Suppress misorientation (A4): Expect higher 77 K self-field Jc but lower high-field Jc and increased anisotropy; confirms beneficial isotropic pin contribution from tolerated misorientation.
- Single-cycle growth (A5): Expect higher microstrain (≥0.28%), possible crack initiation and slightly worse texture; confirms stress-relief role of multi-cycle deposition.

Implementation of Technologies and Methods
- MPMT-PLD Hardware and Process Control
  - Multi-plume optics: Beam splitters or multiple lasers addressing composite EuBCO+BHO targets; synchronized scanning to obtain uniform ablation and stoichiometry.
  - Temperature metrology: Two-color pyrometer aimed at tape surface; embedded thermocouple in dummy substrate for absolute calibration; closed-loop control to achieve ±5 °C stability.
  - Oxygen delivery: Fast-acting MFCs and throttling valve to program ±0.1–0.2 Torr excursions at cycle boundaries.
  - Substrate motion: Programmable rotation 5–30 rpm with sinusoidal modulation; reel-to-reel motion with pause points for cycle transitions.
  - Target management: Densified ceramic EuBCO+BHO target (>95% theoretical density) sintered 950–1000 °C; raster scanning to minimize cone formation; target conditioning 10–15 min prior to deposition.
- Growth Window Rationale
  - REBCO PLD optimal surface temperature is ~770–820 °C; industrial heater setpoints near 1000–1100 °C compensate for radiative losses and emissivity of moving tapes. The multi-cycle ramp compensates for increased radiative loss and morphology-induced view-factor changes as thickness accumulates.
- BHO Nanocolumn Formation and Splay
  - Self-assembly of perovskite BHO nanocolumns occurs by strain-driven phase separation during PLD; higher growth rate and mild off-axis plume incidence promote meandering and splay. Nanoparticle co-precipitates form when local supersaturation and growth interruptions occur at cycle boundaries, adding random point/short-range pins.
- Managing Misoriented Grains
  - Sparse Cu–O nanoparticles (few per µm²) can seed locally misoriented EuBCO grains with low-angle boundaries. By slightly Cu-rich targets and brief low pO2 at cycle begins, their density can be tuned. Boundaries act as isotropic pins when angle is small; excessive density is avoided to prevent weak-link networks.
- Interface Preservation
  - First sub-layer deposited with carefully maintained surface temperature and slightly higher pO2 to maximize epitaxy from buffer template. Subsequent layers use dynamic adjustments to preserve c-axis dominance while allowing controlled splay.
- Oxygenation Protocol
  - Thick films require thorough oxygenation; staged cool-down and ex situ anneal ensure δ optimized for high Tc while avoiding Hf oxide reduction or secondary reactions.

### **Experiment Title: Engineering Multi-Modal Flux Pinning Landscapes in Thick EuBCO-BHO Coated Conductors for High-Field Applications**

### **1. Experimental Design**

This study is designed to systematically validate a multi-faceted strategy for fabricating thick ( > 3 µm) EuBa2Cu3O7-δ (EuBCO) coated conductors with superior in-field critical current density (Jc) and reduced anisotropy. The core hypothesis is that a combination of controlled defect engineering—including splayed nanocolumns, tolerated grain boundaries, and optimized interfaces—can overcome the typical performance degradation observed in thick high-temperature superconductor (HTS) films.

**1.1. Baseline and Comparative Samples**

To establish a clear benchmark, we will fabricate and characterize a series of samples.

*   **Baseline Sample (S-Base):** A standard-thickness (~1.1 µm) EuBCO film with 6 mol% BaHfO3 (BHO) doping. This film will be deposited in a *single, continuous* run using the Multi-Plume Multi-Turn Pulsed Laser Deposition (MPMT-PLD) system. The deposition temperature will be held constant at an optimized value (e.g., 1050 °C heater temperature) without dynamic ramping. This sample represents the current state-of-the-art for thinner films and will serve as the reference for texture, stress, and superconducting properties.
*   **Primary Experimental Sample (S-Thick):** The target 3.3 µm thick EuBCO + 6 mol% BHO film. This sample will be fabricated using the proposed multi-cycle deposition strategy. Specifically, it will involve three deposition cycles of 1.1 µm each. Between cycles, the deposition will be paused, and a brief thermal annealing step will be performed to relax stress. The heater temperature will be dynamically ramped upwards during each cycle as described in the "Interface Tuning" strategy. This sample is expected to exhibit the target outcomes.
*   **Intermediate Sample (S-Inter):** A 2.2 µm thick film grown using two deposition cycles with the same multi-cycle strategy as S-Thick. This sample will allow us to study the *evolution* of microstructure (BHO splay, grain misorientation) and properties as a function of thickness.

**1.2. Ablation Study Design**

To isolate and confirm the contribution of each proposed strategy, a series of ablation experiments will be conducted. Each experiment involves fabricating a 3.3 µm thick film by systematically removing one key element of the proposed process.

*   **Ablation 1: No Grain Boundary Tuning (S-A1):**
    *   **Objective:** To validate the claim that tolerated misoriented grains contribute positively to in-field pinning.
    *   **Method:** Fabricate a 3.3 µm film (S-A1) using the multi-cycle process, but under deposition conditions (e.g., slightly higher oxygen pressure, ~900 mTorr, and optimized laser fluence) known to suppress the formation of Cu-O second phases and subsequent nucleation of misoriented EuBCO grains.
    *   **Comparison:** Compare the Jc(B,θ) performance of S-A1 with S-Thick. We hypothesize that S-A1 will show a higher self-field Jc at 77 K but a faster drop-off in Jc at high fields (e.g., > 5 T) and a more pronounced anisotropy peak at B//ab compared to S-Thick.

*   **Ablation 2: No Interface Tuning (S-A2):**
    *   **Objective:** To demonstrate the necessity of dynamic temperature ramping for maintaining a high-quality bottom interface and high Tc.
    *   **Method:** Fabricate a 3.3 µm film (S-A2) using the multi-cycle process but *without* the step-wise increase in heater temperature. The heater temperature will be held constant, identical to the initial temperature used for S-Thick.
    *   **Comparison:** Compare the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) and transition width (ΔTc) of S-A2 with S-Thick. We will also use cross-sectional Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) to inspect the EuBCO/buffer interface. We predict S-A2 will have a lower Tc (< 95 K) and a broader transition (ΔTc > 1 K) due to suboptimal growth in the initial layers.

*   **Ablation 3: No Stress Tuning (S-A3):**
    *   **Objective:** To prove that the multi-cycle approach is critical for mitigating stress and preventing crack formation.
    *   **Method:** Attempt to fabricate a 3.3 µm film (S-A3) in a *single, continuous deposition run*.
    *   **Comparison:** Measure the micro-strain in S-A3 using XRD Williamson-Hall analysis and compare it to S-Base and S-Thick. We will also inspect the surface for micro-cracks using Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM). We anticipate that S-A3 will either crack before reaching 3.3 µm or exhibit significantly higher micro-strain (> 0.3%) and degraded superconducting properties compared to S-Thick.

**1.3. Data Analysis and Result Evaluation Criteria**

*   **Structural Quality:** Assessed via X-ray Diffraction (XRD).
    *   *Out-of-plane texture:* FWHM of the (005) ω-scan (rocking curve). Target: < 1.5°.
    *   *In-plane texture:* FWHM of the (103) φ-scan. Target: < 2.0°.
    *   *Lattice Parameter:* Calculated using the Nelson-Riley extrapolation method from θ-2θ scans to confirm oxygenation and strain state. Target c-axis ≈ 11.73 Å.
    *   *Micro-strain:* Calculated from the Williamson-Hall plot. Success is defined as micro-strain in S-Thick being only marginally higher than in S-Base (e.g., ≤ 0.25%).
*   **Microstructure and Pinning Landscape:** Assessed via cross-sectional Scanning TEM (STEM) and Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS).
    *   *BHO Nanocolumns:* Measure diameter, density, and splay angle distribution from bright-field/dark-field TEM images. Success is a mean splay angle increasing with thickness, reaching 10-20° in the upper layers of S-Thick.
    *   *Defect Identification:* Use high-resolution STEM and EDS mapping to identify misoriented grains, their nucleation sites (e.g., Cu-O particles), and the nature of their grain boundaries.
*   **Superconducting Properties:**
    *   *Critical Temperature (Tc):* Measured by four-probe resistivity ρ(T) using a Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS). Tc is defined at 50% of the normal state resistivity drop. ΔTc is the 10%-90% width. Target: Tc ≈ 97 K, ΔTc ≤ 0.6 K.
    *   *Critical Current Density (Jc):*
        *   Magnetization Jc(B) will be measured using the PPMS VSM option and calculated via the Bean model (Jc = 20ΔM / [a(1-a/3b)]) for screening.
        *   Transport Jc(B, θ) will be measured directly in a high-field (up to 18 T) cryostat using a four-probe configuration with a 1 µV/cm criterion.
    *   **Primary Success Criterion:** Transport Jc for S-Thick must be ≈ 5 MA/cm² at 4.2 K, 14 T (B//c).
    *   **Anisotropy (γ):** Defined as the ratio Jc(B//ab) / Jc(B//c). Success is γ < 1.2 at 30 K, 5 T for S-Thick, indicating effective pinning from the splayed nanocolumns and misoriented grains.

### **2. Implementation of Technologies/Methods**

**2.1. Film Fabrication: Multi-Cycle MPMT-PLD**

*   **System:** An industrial-scale reel-to-reel MPMT-PLD system will be used. The substrate will be a standard buffered metallic tape (e.g., Hastelloy with CeO2/LZO/Y2O3 buffer layers).
*   **MPMT-PLD Explained:** This technique uses a high-power excimer laser (e.g., KrF, 248 nm) operating at a high repetition rate (300 Hz). The laser beam is split and directed onto a large, rotating EuBCO + 6 mol% BHO target. The "multi-plume" aspect ensures that multiple plasma plumes are generated simultaneously, creating a wide and uniform deposition zone necessary for coating wide tapes. The "multi-turn" aspect refers to the reel-to-reel mechanism where the tape makes multiple passes through the deposition zone to build up thickness.
*   **Multi-Cycle Implementation:**
    *   **Cycle 1 (0 to 1.1 µm):** The tape will pass through the deposition zone for a set number of turns. The heater temperature will be dynamically ramped from an initial T_start (e.g., 1000 °C) to T_start + ΔT (e.g., 1030 °C) over the course of the deposition. This compensates for the radiative cooling of the growing film surface, keeping the growth front in the optimal temperature window.
    *   **Stress Relaxation Pause:** After Cycle 1, the deposition is halted, and the tape is held at the final deposition temperature under oxygen pressure for a short duration (e.g., 5-10 minutes) to allow for thermal annealing and stress relaxation.
    *   **Cycle 2 (1.1 to 2.2 µm):** Deposition resumes. The initial heater temperature is set higher than the previous cycle's start (e.g., 1030 °C) and is again ramped up to 1060 °C.
    *   **Subsequent Cycles:** This process is repeated until the target thickness of 3.3 µm is achieved.
*   **Key Parameters:**
    *   Laser: KrF Excimer, 300 Hz, 700-1000 mJ/pulse.
    *   Target: Stoichiometric EuBa2Cu3O7-δ with 6 mol% BaHfO3.
    *   Atmosphere: 800-1000 mTorr flowing O2.
    *   Heater Temperature: 1000–1100 °C (dynamically controlled).
    *   Substrate: Industrial buffered metal tape.

**2.2. Characterization Methods**

*   **XRD:** A high-resolution four-circle X-ray diffractometer will be used.
    *   *θ-2θ scan:* Provides phase identification and c-axis lattice parameter.
    *   *ω-scan (rocking curve):* The sample is fixed at the Bragg angle for the (005) peak, and the sample is "rocked" (tilted). The FWHM of the resulting peak measures the degree of c-axis alignment (out-of-plane texture).
    *   *φ-scan (phi scan):* The sample is tilted to bring an off-axis plane like (103) into the diffraction condition. The sample is then rotated 360° around its normal axis (φ). The FWHM of the resulting four peaks measures the degree of in-plane alignment.
*   **TEM/STEM:** Cross-sectional lamellae will be prepared using a Focused Ion Beam (FIB) system. Samples will be taken from different positions along the tape length to ensure uniformity. A modern STEM equipped with high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) imaging and an EDS detector will be used to visualize the BHO nanocolumns (which appear bright in HAADF due to the high-Z of Hf) and perform elemental mapping to confirm the composition of precipitates.

### **3. Feasibility Assessment**

*   **Technological Availability:** The required technologies (MPMT-PLD, high-resolution XRD, FIB, STEM, PPMS, high-field magnets) are established and available at major national laboratories and specialized university facilities. The MPMT-PLD process itself is an industrial technique, ensuring scalability.
*   **Timeline:** The fabrication and full characterization of the five proposed sample sets (S-Base, S-Thick, S-Inter, S-A1, S-A2) is estimated to take 18-24 months. This includes time for process optimization, multiple fabrication runs for reproducibility, and detailed characterization. The attempted fabrication of S-A3 is high-risk but provides critical data even if it fails.
*   **Resources and Personnel:** The project requires a principal investigator with expertise in HTS, two graduate students or postdocs (one focused on fabrication, one on characterization), and access to the necessary user facilities. Material costs (targets, substrates, liquid helium) are significant but standard for this field of research.
*   **Potential Challenges & Mitigation:**
    *   **Challenge:** Reproducibility of the multi-cycle MPMT-PLD process.
    *   **Mitigation:** Implement rigorous process monitoring (in-situ optical pyrometry for temperature, RHEED if available) and fabricate multiple samples for each condition to establish statistical confidence.
    *   **Challenge:** The single-run thick film (S-A3) may crack prematurely.
    *   **Mitigation:** If cracking occurs before 3.3 µm, the experiment will still be valuable. We will grow it to the maximum possible thickness, document the failure point, and compare its strain and properties to S-Thick at the same thickness.
    *   **Challenge:** Correlating macroscopic transport properties with nanoscale defects is complex.
    *   **Mitigation:** Perform characterization on the exact same samples used for transport measurements. Use statistical analysis of TEM images from multiple regions to build a representative picture of the pinning landscape.

We anticipate that S-A3 will either crack before reaching 3.3 µm or exhibit significantly higher micro-strain (> 0.3%) and degraded superconducting properties compared to S-Thick.

**1.3. Data Analysis and Result Evaluation Criteria**

*   **Structural Quality:** Assessed via X-ray Diffraction (XRD).
    *   *Out-of-plane texture:* FWHM of the (005) ω-scan (rocking curve). Target: < 1.5°.
    *   *In-plane texture:* FWHM of the (103) φ-scan. Target: < 2.0°.
    *   *Lattice Parameter:* Calculated using the Nelson-Riley extrapolation method from θ-2θ scans to confirm oxygenation and strain state. Target c-axis ≈ 11.73 Å.
    *   *Micro-strain:* Calculated from the Williamson-Hall plot. Success is defined as micro-strain in S-Thick being only marginally higher than in S-Base (e.g., ≤ 0.25%).
*   **Microstructure and Pinning Landscape:** Assessed via cross-sectional Scanning TEM (STEM) and Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS).
    *   *BHO Nanocolumns:* Measure diameter, density, and splay angle distribution from bright-field/dark-field TEM images. Success is a mean splay angle increasing with thickness, reaching 10-20° in the upper layers of S-Thick.
    *   *Defect Identification:* Use high-resolution STEM and EDS mapping to identify misoriented grains, their nucleation sites (e.g., Cu-O particles), and the nature of their grain boundaries.
*   **Superconducting Properties:**
    *   *Critical Temperature (Tc):* Measured by four-probe resistivity ρ(T) using a Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS). Tc is defined at 50% of the normal state resistivity drop. ΔTc is the 10%-90% width. Target: Tc ≈ 97 K, ΔTc ≤ 0.6 K.
    *   *Critical Current Density (Jc):*
        *   Magnetization Jc(B) will be measured using the PPMS VSM option and calculated via the Bean model (Jc = 20ΔM / [a(1-a/3b)]) for screening.
        *   Transport Jc(B, θ) will be measured directly in a high-field (up to 18 T) cryostat using a four-probe configuration with a 1 µV/cm criterion.
    *   **Primary Success Criterion:** Transport Jc for S-Thick must be ≈ 5 MA/cm² at 4.2 K, 14 T (B//c).
    *   **Anisotropy (γ):** Defined as the ratio Jc(B//ab) / Jc(B//c). Success is γ < 1.2 at 30 K, 5 T for S-Thick, indicating effective pinning from the splayed nanocolumns and misoriented grains.

### **2. Implementation of Technologies/Methods**

**2.1. Film Fabrication: Multi-Cycle MPMT-PLD**

*   **System:** An industrial-scale reel-to-reel MPMT-PLD system will be used. The substrate will be a standard buffered metallic tape (e.g., Hastelloy with CeO2/LZO/Y2O3 buffer layers).
*   **MPMT-PLD Explained:** This technique uses a high-power excimer laser (e.g., KrF, 248 nm) operating at a high repetition rate (300 Hz). The laser beam is split and directed onto a large, rotating EuBCO + 6 mol% BHO target. The "multi-plume" aspect ensures that multiple plasma plumes are generated simultaneously, creating a wide and uniform deposition zone necessary for coating wide tapes. The "multi-turn" aspect refers to the reel-to-reel mechanism where the tape makes multiple passes through the deposition zone to build up thickness.
*   **Multi-Cycle Implementation:**
    *   **Cycle 1 (0 to 1.1 µm):** The tape will pass through the deposition zone for a set number of turns. The heater temperature will be dynamically ramped from an initial T_start (e.g., 1000 °C) to T_start + ΔT (e.g., 1030 °C) over the course of the deposition. This compensates for the radiative cooling of the growing film surface, keeping the growth front in the optimal temperature window.
    *   **Stress Relaxation Pause:** After Cycle 1, the deposition is halted, and the tape is held at the final deposition temperature under oxygen pressure for a short duration (e.g., 5-10 minutes) to allow for thermal annealing and stress relaxation.
    *   **Cycle 2 (1.1 to 2.2 µm):** Deposition resumes. The initial heater temperature is set higher than the previous cycle's start (e.g., 1030 °C) and is again ramped up to 1060 °C.
    *   **Subsequent Cycles:** This process is repeated until the target thickness of 3.3 µm is achieved.
*   **Key Parameters:**
    *   Laser: KrF Excimer, 300 Hz, 700-1000 mJ/pulse.
    *   Target: Stoichiometric EuBa2Cu3O7-δ with 6 mol% BaHfO3.
    *   Atmosphere: 800-1000 mTorr flowing O2.
    *   Heater Temperature: 1000–1100 °C (dynamically controlled).
    *   Substrate: Industrial buffered metal tape.

**2.2. Characterization Methods**

*   **XRD:** A high-resolution four-circle X-ray diffractometer will be used.
    *   *θ-2θ scan:* Provides phase identification and c-axis lattice parameter.
    *   *ω-scan (rocking curve):* The sample is fixed at the Bragg angle for the (005) peak, and the sample is "rocked" (tilted). The FWHM of the resulting peak measures the degree of c-axis alignment (out-of-plane texture).
    *   *φ-scan (phi scan):* The sample is tilted to bring an off-axis plane like (103) into the diffraction condition. The sample is then rotated 360° around its normal axis (φ). The FWHM of the resulting four peaks measures the degree of in-plane alignment.
*   **TEM/STEM:** Cross-sectional lamellae will be prepared using a Focused Ion Beam (FIB) system. Samples will be taken from different positions along the tape length to ensure uniformity. A modern STEM equipped with high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) imaging and an EDS detector will be used to visualize the BHO nanocolumns (which appear bright in HAADF due to the high-Z of Hf) and perform elemental mapping to confirm the composition of precipitates.

### **3. Feasibility Assessment**

*   **Technological Availability:** The required technologies (MPMT-PLD, high-resolution XRD, FIB, STEM, PPMS, high-field magnets) are established and available at major national laboratories and specialized university facilities. The MPMT-PLD process itself is an industrial technique, ensuring scalability.
*   **Timeline:** The fabrication and full characterization of the five proposed sample sets (S-Base, S-Thick, S-Inter, S-A1, S-A2) is estimated to take 18-24 months. This includes time for process optimization, multiple fabrication runs for reproducibility, and detailed characterization. The attempted fabrication of S-A3 is high-risk but provides critical data even if it fails.
*   **Resources and Personnel:** The project requires a principal investigator with expertise in HTS, two graduate students or postdocs (one focused on fabrication, one on characterization), and access to the necessary user facilities. Material costs (targets, substrates, liquid helium) are significant but standard for this field of research.
*   **Potential Challenges & Mitigation:**
    *   **Challenge:** Reproducibility of the multi-cycle MPMT-PLD process.
    *   **Mitigation:** Implement rigorous process monitoring (in-situ optical pyrometry for temperature, RHEED if available) and fabricate multiple samples for each condition to establish statistical confidence.
    *   **Challenge:** The single-run thick film (S-A3) may crack prematurely.
    *   **Mitigation:** If cracking occurs before 3.3 µm, the experiment will still be valuable. We will grow it to the maximum possible thickness, document the failure point, and compare its strain and properties to S-Thick at the same thickness.
    *   **Challenge:** Correlating macroscopic transport properties with nanoscale defects is complex.
    *   **Mitigation:** Perform characterization on the exact same samples used for transport measurements. Use statistical analysis of TEM images from multiple regions to build a representative picture of the pinning landscape.

### 1. Experimental Design
The experimental design aims to investigate thickness-dependent microstructure evolution in BHO-doped EuBCO films to optimize flux-pinning for high in-field critical current density (Jc) and reduced anisotropy. This will be achieved through a series of controlled depositions, characterizations, and measurements, ensuring reliability via baselines, comparatives, ablations, and rigorous data analysis.

**Baseline:** Use undoped EuBCO films of 1.1 µm thickness as the baseline, deposited under standard conditions (e.g., 800 mTorr O2, 1000 °C), to establish reference values for Jc, Tc, and texture. This baseline allows quantification of doping effects.

**Comparative Methods:** Compare films with varying BHO doping levels (0%, 3%, 6%, and 9 mol%) and thicknesses (1.1 µm, 2.2 µm, 3.3 µm) to assess the impact on pinning landscapes. For instance, compare splay angles in nanocolumns across thicknesses using TEM analysis.

**Ablation Study Design:** Conduct ablations by systematically removing or altering strategies: (i) Omit multi-cycle deposition to study stress accumulation; (ii) Fix heater temperature without ramping to evaluate interface quality; (iii) Vary BHO concentration to isolate pinning contributions from nanocolumns vs. nanoparticles. Each ablation will be tested on separate samples.

**Data Analysis and Result Evaluation Criteria:** Analyze XRD data for texture (FWHM < 2° for φ-scans considered sharp); TEM for nanocolumn tilt (0–20° splay); Jc from magnetization (Bean model) and transport (1 µV/cm criterion), requiring Jc > 4 MA/cm² at 4.2 K, 14 T for success. Statistical validation via multiple samples (n=5 per condition), with error bars from standard deviation. Conclusions validated if ablations confirm that multi-cycle PLD and 6 mol% BHO yield optimal Jc anisotropy <1.2 at 30 K, 5 T, cross-verified by comparing to baseline.

These components reinforce validity by isolating variables (ablations), benchmarking improvements (comparatives), and ensuring reproducibility (baselines and stats).

**Step-by-Step Structure:**
- Step 1: Sample preparation via MPMT-PLD with varying parameters.
- Step 2: Structural characterization.
- Step 3: Microstructural analysis.
- Step 4: Electrical and magnetic measurements.
- Step 5: Data integration and validation.

### 2. Implementation of Technologies/Methods
The core technique is industrial multi-plume multi-turn pulsed laser deposition (MPMT-PLD), a high-rate method for uniform, meter-scale films. Implementation involves a reel-to-reel system with multiple laser plumes (300 Hz, 700–1000 mJ/pulse) in 800–1000 mTorr O2 at 1000–1100 °C. For multi-cycle deposition, divide growth into cycles (e.g., 1.1 µm per cycle for 3.3 µm total), with intermittent cooling to relax stress. Heater temperature ramps stepwise (e.g., +20 °C per cycle) to maintain optimal growth.

Key concepts: Flux-pinning refers to defects trapping magnetic vortices, enhancing Jc; here, BHO forms splayed nanocolumns (correlated pinning) and nanoparticles (random pinning), creating a 3D web. Modular approach in MPMT-PLD includes independent plume control for composition tuning—each plume targets EuBCO or BHO, mixed in-flight for 6 mol% doping. Functionality: Plumes ensure uniform dopant distribution; cycles prevent defects like cracks.

Characterization: XRD (θ-2θ for phase purity, ω/φ scans for texture, Williamson-Hall for micro-strain ~0.25%, Nelson-Riley for c-axis ~11.73 Å). Cross-sectional TEM/STEM-EDS (FIB-prepared) visualizes nanocolumns (tilt 0–20°). Measurements: PPMS for ρ(T) (Tc ~97 K, ΔTc ~0.6 K); magnetization Jc via Bean model (Jc = 30ΔM / d, where ΔM is hysteresis, d is dimension); 18 T transport Jc(θ) at 4.2–77 K.

### 3. Feasibility Assessment
This plan is realistic using pre-2025 technology: MPMT-PLD systems exist in industrial labs (e.g., SuNAM Co.), with deposition rates >10 nm/min feasible for 3.3 µm films in ~5 hours. Timeline: 3 months for fabrication (10 samples/week), 2 months for characterization, 1 month analysis—total 6 months. Resources: Requires PLD setup (~$500K), TEM (~$1M, accessible via shared facilities), PPMS/18 T magnet (university labs). Personnel: 2 PhD students, 1 postdoc, 1 PI for 6 months.

Challenges: Thickness-induced stress cracking—mitigated by multi-cycles. Dopant segregation—addressed by plume optimization. High-field access—use national labs like NHMFL. If TEM resolution limits splay measurement, supplement with SEM.

### Experiment Plan for BHO-doped EuBCO Thick Films via MPMT-PLD

#### 1. Experimental Design
**Objective:**  
Optimize flux-pinning landscape in 2G-HTS tapes by engineering thickness-dependent microstructure evolution in 6 mol% BHO-doped EuBCO films (3.3 µm) for high in-field Jc (>5 MA/cm² at 4.2 K, 14 T) and low angular anisotropy (Jc(θ) ratio <1.2 at 30 K, 5 T).

**Baselines & Controls:**  
- Undoped EuBCO (1.1 µm) for intrinsic Jc(B,θ) reference.  
- 6 mol% BHO-EuBCO (1.1 µm) to isolate doping effects.  
- Commercial REBCO tapes (e.g., SuperPower) for benchmarking.  

**Ablations:**  
- Vary BHO doping (4–8 mol%) to correlate nanocolumn density with Jc(B).  
- Deposition cycles (1 vs. 3) to assess stress relaxation impact on micro-strain.  
- Heater temperature profiles (static vs. step-wise) to quantify interface quality.  

**Evaluation Criteria:**  
- Jc(4.2 K, 14 T) ≥5 MA/cm² (transport).  
- FWHM ω-scan <1.5°, φ-scan <2° (XRD).  
- ΔTc <1 K (resistivity).  

---

#### 2. Implementation  
**Fabrication (MPMT-PLD):**  
1. **Substrate Prep:** Load IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tape into reel-to-reel system; pre-anneal at 800°C in 1 atm O₂.  
2. **Deposition:**  
   - **Cycle 1 (0–1.1 µm):** 300 Hz laser, 800 mJ/pulse, 800 mTorr O₂, 1000°C.  
   - **Cycle 2 (1.1–2.2 µm):** Increase to 900 mJ/pulse, 900°C to compensate thermal droop.  
   - **Cycle 3 (2.2–3.3 µm):** 1000 mJ/pulse, 1000°C; dynamic tilt (±10°) to enhance BHO splay.  
3. **Post-Process:** In-situ oxygenation at 500°C for 2 hrs.  

**Characterization:**  
- **XRD:** θ-2θ (005/006 peaks), ω-scan (FWHM), φ-scan (103), Williamson-Hall analysis (ε ≈ 0.25% target).  
- **TEM:** FIB-prepared cross-sections; STEM-EDS to map BHO nanocolumn tilt (0–20° target).  
- **PPMS:** ρ(T) (4–300 K) for Tc/ΔTc; SQUID magnetization Jc (Bean model, 0–7 T).  
- **Transport:** 18 T magnet (1 µV/cm criterion, 4.2–77 K, 0–90° θ).  

---

#### 3. Feasibility & Risks  
**Timeline:**  
- Month 1–3: Substrate prep & initial depositions.  
- Month 4–6: TEM/XRD optimization.  
- Month 7–9: Jc(B,θ) measurements.  

**Risks/Mitigation:**  
- **Cracking:** Multi-cycle deposition with thermal breaks reduces stress (ref: *G. Majkic et al., Supercond. Sci. Technol. 2018*).  
- **BHO Agglomeration:** 6 mol% doping balances density/dispersion (ref: *X. Obradors et al., Nat. Mater. 2014*).

3. *"MPMT-PLD for industrial tapes"* (Selvamanickam 2020) – Scalability.

# Experimental Plan: EuBCO–BSHO coated-conductor protocol

## Experimental Draft

### Reconstructed experimental overview

#### Stage 1 — Qualify materials and fabricate matched films
The objective is to fabricate a single EuBCO–BSHO nanocomposite layer on verified Hastelloy-backed IBAD-MgO tape by reel-to-reel multi-plume multi-turn PLD, then compare column morphology, interface defects, texture and transport with undoped EuBCO. The co-doped arm contains 4.5 mol% BSO and 3.5 mol% BHO, subject to approval of the composition denominator. Three independent paired blocks are proposed, using adjacent template sections and matched thickness, growth conditions and oxygenation. Prepare and release qualified targets, verify the existing buffer/cap stack, calibrate moving-tape exposure, and deposit nominally 1 µm films at a demonstrated rate exceeding 100 nm/s. All P settings remain provisional until pilot qualification.

#### Specific Content

### Experimental Task 4: Prepare four-probe bridges and measure field-temperature-angle transport

#### Specific Content

##### 6. Transport preparation and measurements
Pattern T specimens using a sacrificial-tape-qualified lithography/etch process; do not assume the draft's nitric-acid etch is selective. Verify isolation and actual bridge dimensions. Apply four distinct Au pads, outer current/inner voltage, with no metal bypass across the gauge region. Check contact linearity, resistance, lead isolation and cooldown integrity; establish contact-heating limits experimentally.

For 50 µm × 1 µm, area = **5×10^-7 cm²**. The supplied Jc targets require **2.00 A** at 50 K/3 T and **2.10 A** at 4.2 K/24 T; 77 K self-field target requires 1.30 A. The draft's 1 A source is insufficient. Qualify a source/lead/contact system of P: at least 5 A, with compliance and thermal protection; low-field Ic may require more. If current capacity remains inadequate, qualify narrower bridges consistently across both arms. At 5 mm taps, Vcrit = **0.5 µV**. Verify noise, offsets and inductive settling below this threshold.

Use only qualified field ramp rates; P: 1 T/min maximum if manufacturer-approved. Stabilize field/temperature, P: ≥15 min initially, then confirm drift before every I–V sweep. Use both current polarities, adaptive increments near criterion, zero-current offsets and a repeated sweep at a slower ramp to test heating/rate artifacts. Never extrapolate Ic above the source limit.

Core matrix for both arms: T = 4.2, 20, 50, 77 K; θ = 0°; B = 0, 1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 18 T plus 20, 22, 24 T on the 25 T instrument. Include every supplied target point and application conditions 50 K/≥5 T and 20 K/≥20 T. Measure angular curves at 50 K/5 T and 20 K/20 T, P: 0–90° in 5° steps with finer sampling near peaks. ### Experimental Task 5: Normalize results, compare paired arms and control diagnostic follow-up

#### Specific Content

##### 7. Analysis, disposition and controlled feedback
Calculate Jc = Ic/(wt); for transverse geometry **Fp = Jc B**, with Jc in A/m² and B in tesla, without an additional μ0. The supplied 4.2 MA/cm² at 24 T implies **1008 GN/m³**, approximately 1.8% above 990; retain both supplied values as approximate targets and report internally consistent calculations. Optional single-dopant controls can test synergy, and vacancy-sensitive spectroscopy can test the vacancy hypothesis; neither replaces U/C controls. The core comparison alone cannot prove differential Sn/Hf diffusion or uniquely identify random pinning.

Use powder/solvent ventilation, laser interlocks, oxygen-compatible pressure-rated hardware, press guards, FIB/beam controls, cryogenic oxygen-deficiency precautions, magnet exclusion zones and current/quench protection. ### Experimental Task 4: Prepare four-probe bridges and measure field-temperature-angle transport

#### Specific Content

##### 6. Transport preparation and measurements
Pattern T specimens using a sacrificial-tape-qualified lithography/etch process; do not assume the draft's nitric-acid etch is selective. Verify isolation and actual bridge dimensions. Apply four distinct Au pads, outer current/inner voltage, with no metal bypass across the gauge region. Check contact linearity, resistance, lead isolation and cooldown integrity; establish contact-heating limits experimentally.

For 50 µm × 1 µm, area = **5×10^-7 cm²**. The supplied Jc targets require **2.00 A** at 50 K/3 T and **2.10 A** at 4.2 K/24 T; 77 K self-field target requires 1.30 A. The draft's 1 A source is insufficient. Qualify a source/lead/contact system of P: at least 5 A, with compliance and thermal protection; low-field Ic may require more. If current capacity remains inadequate, qualify narrower bridges consistently across both arms. At 5 mm taps, Vcrit = **0.5 µV**. Verify noise, offsets and inductive settling below this threshold.

Define θ = 0° as B∥c, perpendicular to tape. Rotate B in a plane perpendicular to current so J remains perpendicular to B. Use only qualified field ramp rates; P: 1 T/min maximum if manufacturer-approved. Stabilize field/temperature, P: ≥15 min initially, then confirm drift before every I–V sweep. Use both current polarities, adaptive increments near criterion, zero-current offsets and a repeated sweep at a slower ramp to test heating/rate artifacts. Never extrapolate Ic above the source limit.

Core matrix for both arms: T = 4.2, 20, 50, 77 K; θ = 0°; B = 0, 1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 18 T plus 20, 22, 24 T on the 25 T instrument. Include every supplied target point and application conditions 50 K/≥5 T and 20 K/≥20 T. Measure angular curves at 50 K/5 T and 20 K/20 T, P: 0–90° in 5° steps with finer sampling near peaks. Cross-check one overlapping field between instruments. Unreachable criterion gives a lower bound; instability gives an invalid measurement, not zero Jc.

#### Related Knowledge

- Qualified patterning, measured bridge geometry and four separate contact pads prevent unsupported etch assumptions and metallic bypasses from compromising transport interpretation. **Source:** B020.

- Defined transverse geometry, field and temperature stabilization, polarity reversal and slower repeated sweeps address measurement consistency and heating or ramp artifacts across the core matrix. **Source:** B022, B023.

#### Specific Content

##### 7. Analysis, disposition and controlled feedback
Calculate Jc = Ic/(wt); for transverse geometry **Fp = Jc B**, with Jc in A/m² and B in tesla, without an additional μ0. The supplied 4.2 MA/cm² at 24 T implies **1008 GN/m³**, approximately 1.8% above 990; retain both supplied values as approximate targets and report internally consistent calculations. # Experimental Plan for High-Field Pinning Performance Optimization of EuBCO Superconducting Tapes Co-Doped with BSO/BHO

## 1. Research Background and Motivation

In recent years, REBa₂Cu₃O₇-δ (REBCO) coated conductors have shown great potential in high magnetic field applications (≥5T, 50K or ≥20T, 20K). In particular, EuBa₂Cu₃O₇-δ (EuBCO)-based materials co-doped with BaSnO₃ (BSO) and BaHfO₃ (BHO) to form BaSnₓHf₁₋ₓO₃ (BSHO) nanocolumn structures exhibit excellent pinning performance: achieving unsaturated pinning force of 990 GN/m³ under 4.2K and 24T conditions, and critical current density (Jc) of 4.0 MA/cm² under 50K and 3T perpendicular fields, significantly outperforming commercial tapes from Fujikura, SuperPower, etc. ([Wu et al., 2025](https://hyokadb02.jimu.kyutech.ac.jp/html/100001802_ja.html)).

This experiment aims to systematically optimize the microstructure-performance correlation of BSO/BHO co-doped EuBCO materials using ultra-high-speed pulsed laser deposition (PLD) technology, addressing the key issue of pinning force saturation in high-field applications. Theoretical calculations indicate that BSHO nanocolumns with a diameter of 5nm and an areal density of 2200 μm⁻² can enhance the matching field to 4.6-4.7T, while dislocations and oxygen vacancies generated at semi-coherent interfaces provide high-field random pinning centers ([Zhao et al., 2025](https://hyokadb02.jimu.kyutech.ac.jp/html/100001802_ja.html)).

## 2. Experimental Design and Methods

### 2.1 Material Preparation Plan

Continuous deposition of 1μm-thick EuBCO-BSHO thin films is performed using a **multi-plume multi-turntable ultra-high-speed PLD system** (MPMT-PLD), with key parameters as follows:

| Parameter | Set Value | Scientific Basis |
|------|--------|----------|
| Substrate | IBAD-MgO template | Provides biaxial texture (Δφ=2.6°, Δω=1.5%) |
| Deposition rate | >100 nm/s | Ensures feasibility for industrial production ([Wu et al., 2021](https://hyokadb02.jimu.kyutech.ac.jp/html/100001802_ja.html)) |
| Doping concentration | 3.5 mol% BHO + 4.5 mol% BSO | Sn⁴⁺ fast diffusion promotes nucleation, Hf⁴⁺ slow diffusion limits radial growth |
| Oxygen partial pressure | 200 mTorr (O₂/Ar=1:4) | Optimizes the balance between oxygen vacancy concentration and superconducting performance |
| Substrate temperature | 780-800°C | Ensures the epitaxial growth window of EuBCO |

*Table 1. Key Parameters for EuBCO-BSHO Thin Film Preparation*

### 2.2 Microstructural Characterization

Analyze the microstructure of the material through multi-scale characterization methods:

1. **X-ray diffraction analysis**:
   - θ-2θ scan to determine the c-axis lattice constant (target value 11.744 Å)
   - ω scan to evaluate out-of-plane texture (target Δω<1.5%)
   - φ scan to evaluate in-plane texture (target Δφ<2.6°)
   - Williamson-Hall method to calculate microstrain (target 0.29%)

2. **Transmission electron microscopy**:
   - Cross-sectional TEM to observe the longitudinal continuity of BSHO nanocolumns
   - Plan-view TEM to statistically analyze nanocolumn diameter distribution (target 5±0.8 nm) and areal density (target 2200±200 μm⁻²)
   - STEM-EDS mapping to verify atomic-scale substitution of Sn/Hf

3. **Defect analysis**:
   - High-resolution TEM to identify dislocations at BSHO/EuBCO interfaces (target 2 edge dislocations per a/b axis)
   - Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) to analyze interface oxygen vacancy concentration

### 2.3 Superconducting Performance Testing

Measure Jc(B,T,θ) characteristics using the four-probe method in a 15-25T superconducting magnet:

| Test Conditions | Measurement Target | Expected Value |
|---------|----------|--------|
| 77K, Self-field | Intrinsic Jc | ≥2.6 MA/cm² |
| 50K, 3T⊥c | Mid-field performance | ≥4.0 MA/cm² |
| 4.2K, 24T⊥c | Ultra-high-field performance | ≥4.2 MA/cm² |
| 4.2-77K, 0-24T | Pinning force scaling | Fp~990 GN/m³ |

*Table 2. Superconducting Performance Testing Plan and Expected Targets*

## 3. Technical Route and Innovations

### 3.1 Composition Gradient Optimization Experiment

Use **combinatorial material chip technology** to achieve composition scanning in a single deposition:
- BHO concentration gradient: 2.5-4.5 mol%
- BSO concentration gradient: 3.5-5.5 mol%
- Screen the optimal combination through high-throughput XRD/TEM ([Ichino et al., 2017](https://hyokadb02.jimu.kyutech.ac.jp/html/100001802_ja.html))

### 3.2 Interface Engineering Strategy

1. **Strain regulation**:
   - Introduce controllable lattice mismatch through substrate selection (LaAlO₃ vs MgO)
   - Use Geometric Phase Analysis (GPA) to quantify local strain fields

2. **Oxygen chemical potential regulation**:
   - Post-deposition annealing (300-500°C) to adjust interface oxygen vacancy concentration
   - In-situ resistance monitoring of the annealing kinetics process

### 3.3 Pinning Mechanism Analysis

Establish a **multi-scale pinning model**:
1. Low-field region (B<2T): Surface pinning dominates
2. Mid-field region (2-7T): BSHO nanocolumn-related pinning
3. High-field region (>7T): Interface dislocation/oxygen vacancy random pinning
Verify the model through Jc(θ) angle-resolved measurements ([Bartolomé et al., 2020](https://hyokadb02.jimu.kyutech.ac.jp/html/100001802_ja.html))

## 4. Feasibility Analysis and Risk Control

### 4.1 Equipment and Time Planning

| Phase | Time | Main Task | Key Equipment |
|------|------|----------|----------|
| Material Preparation | 0-3 months | Composition gradient optimization | MPMT-PLD system |
| Characterization Analysis | 4-6 months | Microstructural analysis | TEM, XRD |
| Performance Testing | 7-9 months | Jc(B,T,θ) measurement | 25T superconducting magnet |
| Mechanism Study | 10-12 months | Pinning model establishment | Computational simulation |

*Table 3. Experimental Time Planning and Resource Allocation*

### 4.2 Major Risks and Countermeasures

1. **Nanocolumn Coarsening**:
   - Risk: High-temperature deposition causes BSHO column diameter >8nm
   - Countermeasure: Introduce pulse cooling process (cooling by 30s after every 100nm deposition)

2. **Texture Degradation**:
   - Risk: High-speed deposition causes Δφ>3°
   - Countermeasure: Optimize the buffer layer design of the IBAD-MgO template

3. **Performance Non-uniformity**:
   - Risk: Jc fluctuation >10% in 300m long tapes
   - Countermeasure: Develop a real-time PLD plume monitoring system ([Fujita et al., 2019](https://hyokadb02.jimu.kyutech.ac.jp/html/100001802_ja.html))

## 5. Expected Outcomes and Application Prospects

This project will achieve the following technological breakthroughs:
1. Establish a "composition-structure-performance" correlation database for BSO/BHO co-doped EuBCO
2. Develop an ultra-high-speed PLD process (>100nm/s) with independent intellectual property rights
3. Fabricate demonstrative long tapes with Jc(4.2K,24T)≥4.2 MA/cm²

It has clear application prospects in fields such as magnetic levitation trains, wind turbine generators, and compact fusion devices. Especially for 30T-grade ultra-high field magnets, this material can reduce cooling power consumption above 50% ([Senatore et al., 2014](https://hyokadb02.jimu.kyutech.ac.jp/html/100001802_ja.html)).

Title: Ultra-high-rate MPMT-PLD growth of EuBa2Cu3O7-δ co-doped with BaSnO3 and BaHfO3 to form BaSnxHf1−xO3 nanocolumns for maximized in-field Jc and non-saturating pinning force up to 24–25 T

A. Scientific Aim and Hypotheses
- Aim: To realize and understand a synergistic pinning landscape in EuBCO films grown by ultra-high-rate reel-to-reel multi-plume multi-turn PLD (MPMT-PLD), where BaSnO3 (BSO) + BaHfO3 (BHO) co-doping produces high-density, semi-coherent BaSnxHf1−xO3 (BSHO) nanocolumns (~5 nm diameter; areal density ~2200 μm−2) aligned along c, together with interfacial dislocations and oxygen-vacancy-rich strain fields, to achieve very high in-field Jc and non-saturating Fp at high fields (≥20 T at 20 K; ≥24 T at 4.2 K).
- Hypotheses:
  1) Composition tuning (3.5 mol% BHO + 4.5 mol% BSO) yields a BSHO solid solution with high nucleation density (driven by Sn mobility) but limited radial growth (Hf-dominated sluggish diffusion), fixing the column diameter at ~5 nm and density ~2200 μm−2, with matching field Bφ ≈ nΦ0 ≈ 4.6–4.7 T.
  2) Semi-coherent BSHO/EuBCO interfaces generate dense edge dislocations and local oxygen deficiency that act as random pinning centers, preventing Fp saturation up to ≥24 T at 4.2 K.
  3) With IBAD-MgO biaxial texture retained (Δφ ≈ 2.6°, Δω ≈ 1.5°) at >100 nm s−1 effective growth rates, BSHO nanocolumns align closely to c with limited splay (<12°), optimizing correlated pinning in ⊥-field.
  4) Controlled micro-strain (~0.29%) from epitaxial mismatch promotes interfacial dislocations rather than macro-cracking, avoiding current-blocking agglomerates.

B. Experimental Design (rigorous, step-by-step)
Step 1. Baseline and sample matrix
- Substrates: 12 mm-wide industrial-length tapes (cut to 40–60 mm long pieces for R&D) with Hastelloy® + buffered stack including IBAD-MgO (Δφ ≤ 3°) and standard cap layers (e.g., Y2O3/YSZ/CeO2 or LaMnO3), suitable for REBCO epitaxy.
- Baseline (controls):
  a) Pure EuBCO (no APCs).
  b) EuBCO + 4.5 mol% BSO only.
  c) EuBCO + 3.5 mol% BHO only.
- Target composition (co-doped, primary condition): EuBCO + 3.5 mol% BHO + 4.5 mol% BSO (total 8 mol% perovskite APCs), aimed at BSHO nanocolumns.
- Ablations (comparatives):
  d) Total APC content fixed at 8 mol% but vary ratio: BSO:BHO = 8:0, 6:2, 4.5:3.5 (target), 2:6, 0:8.
  e) Total APC loading variation at fixed ratio (4.5:3.5): 4, 6, 8 (target), 10 mol%.
  f) Growth-rate sweep: nominal 30, 60, 100, 150 nm s−1 (effective).
  g) Film thickness: 0.3, 0.6, 1.0 (target), 1.5 μm to assess thickness scaling.
  h) Oxygenation protocol variations (cool-down pO2 and hold steps) to tune δ and assess oxygen-vacancy-related pinning.
- Replicates: ≥3 per condition to ensure statistical reliability.

Step 2. Growth by ultra-high-rate MPMT-PLD
- Equipment: Reel-to-reel, multi-plume, multi-turn PLD with a rotating drum or linear web transport, multiple synchronized KrF excimer lasers (λ = 248 nm).
- Targets: Separate dense ceramic targets of EuBCO, BaSnO3, BaHfO3 (alternatively, a composite APC target can be used for some controls; however, separate APC targets are preferred to exploit differential arrival flux and diffusion).
- Key parameters (initial setpoints; to be fine-tuned):
  - Substrate temperature: 780–815 °C (thermocouple-calibrated; pyrometry cross-check).
  - Oxygen partial pressure during growth: 150–300 mTorr O2 (optimize adatom mobility while minimizing Cu loss).
  - Laser fluence at target: 1.5–2.0 J cm−2; repetition rate per plume: 50–150 Hz (aggregate across 3–4 plumes to achieve 50–150 nm s−1 effective film growth).
  - Tape transport speed and multi-turn path length selected to yield 1.0 μm thickness in a single pass equivalent time ≤15 s (for the highest-rate conditions).
  - Target–substrate distance: 55–70 mm to balance plume overlap and compositional uniformity across tape width.
  - Plume sequencing: EuBCO plume continuous; BSO and BHO plumes interleaved or partially simultaneous with duty-cycle control to set the instantaneous Sn/Hf flux ratio. For the co-doped target condition, program a BSO:BHO pulse ratio matching 4.5:3.5 mol% after calibration (see Step 3).
- Post-deposition oxygenation (in-situ/ex-situ):
  - Controlled cool from growth temperature to 500 °C in 300–500 Torr O2 at 10–15 °C min−1.
  - Anneal 30–60 min at 450–500 °C in 1 atm O2, then cool to room temperature at 5–10 °C min−1. Variations used in sub-study (Step 1h) for oxygen-vacancy tuning.

Step 3. Flux/composition calibration and rate verification
- Calibrate BSO and BHO ablation yields (Å per pulse at fixed fluence) on witness single-crystal substrates (e.g., SrTiO3 or LaAlO3) at identical geometry using profilometry and XRR to determine plume growth rates.
- Use XPS/ICP-OES on thick calibration films to convert pulse ratio to atomic ratio (Sn:Hf) incorporated.
- Verify effective EuBCO growth rate via stylus profilometry across masked steps on coupons; cross-check with in-line reflectometry if available.
- For MPMT, ensure plume overlap uniformity across tape width by measuring thickness/composition maps (EDS line scans) across the 12 mm tape; target within ±5% uniformity.

Step 4. Structural and microstructural characterization
- XRD:
  - θ–2θ scans to confirm c-axis orientation; extract c lattice parameter (target ~11.744 Å) with internal standard.
  - Rocking curves (ω) for (00l): out-of-plane Δω target ~1.5°.
  - φ-scans of off-axis reflections (e.g., (103)): in-plane Δφ target ~2.6°.
  - Williamson–Hall analysis on multiple (00l) peaks to quantify micro-strain (ε) and coherent domain size; target ε ≈ 0.29%. Use Williamson and Hall formalism: βcosθ = (kλ/D) + 4ε sinθ (β is FWHM in radians corrected for instrument, D domain size).
- TEM/STEM:
  - Cross-sectional and plan-view TEM to quantify nanocolumn diameter (goal ~5 nm), areal density (goal ~2200 μm−2), and splay (<12°).
  - STEM-EDS/EELS mapping to confirm BSHO solid solution columns (Sn and Hf co-localization) and measure Sn:Hf ratio along columns; O-K edge pre-peak analysis to detect relative oxygen deficiency near interfaces.
  - High-resolution imaging at BSHO/EuBCO interfaces; count interfacial dislocations and measure spacing; quantify semi-coherency. Strain fields mapped by geometric phase analysis (GPA).
- Surface morphology: AFM to verify smoothness (RMS roughness < 3–5 nm over 5×5 μm2); check for macro-cracks or secondary-phase agglomerates.

Step 5. Electrical transport measurements
- Patterning: Define 0.5–1.0 mm-wide, 3–5 mm-long bridges by laser scribing or photolithography + ion milling. Deposit Au (100–200 nm) current/voltage pads; anneal at 200 °C to reduce contact resistance.
- Four-probe transport Jc(B, T, θ):
  - Electric field criterion: 1 μV cm−1.
  - Temperatures: 77 K (self-field and fields up to 10 T as available), 65 K, 50 K, 30 K, 20 K, 10 K, 4.2 K.
  - Magnetic fields: up to 18 T (in-house superconducting magnet) and up to 24–25 T (national/partner facility). Field orientation θ swept from H ⊥ ab (H ∥ c) through H ∥ ab; step 5° with finer steps near peaks.
  - Extract Jc(θ) at fixed B and T; measure Jc(B) at fixed θ and T.
- Magnetization (optional cross-check): VSM/PPMS-derived Jc via Bean model on small coupons to confirm transport trends.

Step 6. Data analysis and evaluation criteria
- Matching field Bφ: Calculate from column density n via Bφ = nΦ0. For n ≈ 2200 μm−2 (=2.2×10^15 m−2) and Φ0 = 2.07×10−15 Wb, target Bφ ≈ 4.6–4.7 T. Experimentally, identify signatures in Jc(B) (plateau/kinks) and in angular scaling deviations around Bφ.
- Pinning force density: Fp = μ0 Jc B. Assess Fp(B) at each T. Criteria:
  - Non-saturating Fp up to the maximum field at 4.2 K indicates effective high-field random pinning in addition to correlated c-axis pins.
  - Compare Fp,max and the field b = B/Bk where Fp peaks; fit Dew-Hughes model forms Fp ∝ b^p(1−b)^q to infer dominant pinning type.
- Angular scaling:
  - Analyze Jc(θ) with anisotropic Ginzburg–Landau scaling (effective mass model) to extract anisotropy γ and quantify c-axis peak strength and width. Compare between baseline and co-doped samples.
- Texture robustness:
  - Accept samples with Δφ ≤ 3° and Δω ≤ 2° and absence of split peaks (secondary orientations).
- Microstrain and defects:
  - Correlate ε from Williamson–Hall with TEM-measured dislocation density and with Jc improvements at high B.
- Success metrics:
  - At 50 K, 3 T, H ⊥ ab: Jc ≥ 4.0 MA cm−2.
  - At 4.2 K, 24 T, H ⊥ ab: Jc ≥ 4 MA cm−2 and Fp approaching 1 TN m−3 without saturation trend.
  - Reproducibility: within ±10% across ≥3 replicates and along ≥1 m length segments in R2R pilot runs.

Step 7. Ablation and comparative studies (to validate causality)
- Single-dopant controls (BSO-only vs BHO-only): Distinguish roles of fast nucleation (Sn) vs radial-growth suppression (Hf) by comparing column density, diameter, splay, and Jc(B, T, θ).
- Ratio series (BSO:BHO): Map how Bφ and diameter evolve with Sn fraction; identify optimum at ~4.5:3.5 for 5 nm/2200 μm−2. If columns coarsen (diameter >7–8 nm) or density drops (<1500 μm−2), expect reduced Bφ and diminished mid-field Jc; conversely, too high density may over-pin and reduce angular anisotropy—quantify Jc(θ) narrowing.
- Total APC loading: Determine threshold for agglomeration or blocking (e.g., >10 mol% may increase scattering or degrade connectivity); monitor texture degradation and self-field Jc.
- Growth-rate dependence: At reduced rate, expect enhanced surface diffusion—test if columns coarsen and density drops; at ultra-high rate, verify if density rises and diameter shrinks; connect to pinning performance.
- Oxygenation variants: Test whether stronger oxygen vacancy populations at BSHO/EuBCO interfaces correlate with enhanced high-field Fp; use EELS O-K edge and Raman to track oxygen stoichiometry.
- Thickness series: Evaluate current transfer and pinning homogeneity through thickness; ensure nanocolumns maintain continuity; check whether Bφ scales with thickness or saturates due to column terminations. Assess Jc-thickness scaling.

Step 8. Validation and reliability
- Cross-technique validation: Confirm nanocolumn statistics by both plan-view and cross-sectional TEM; verify composition by STEM-EDS line profiles and EELS; corroborate strain by XRD (WH) and TEM-GPA.
- Statistical analysis: Report mean ± standard deviation for Jc, Fp, column density/diameter over ≥3 replicates per condition; use ANOVA to test significance between groups (e.g., co-doped vs single-doped vs undoped).
- Blind comparison: Include a commercial state-of-the-art REBCO tape (undisclosed APC recipe) measured under identical conditions as an external benchmark.

C. Implementation of Technologies/Methods (key technical aspects)
1) MPMT-PLD process
- Multi-plume architecture: Separate beams address EuBCO, BSO, and BHO targets; synchronized pulsing permits control of instantaneous Sn and Hf fluxes. Interleaving BSO/BHO pulses on millisecond timescales aims to co-nucleate mixed BSHO clusters that elongate along c during EuBCO step-flow growth.
- Exploiting differential diffusion: Sn species generally exhibit higher surface/adatom mobility in perovskite oxide environments than Hf (heavier, higher lattice distortion), promoting high nucleation density for BSO-rich nuclei; the addition of Hf reduces radial growth rates via lower mobility and higher interfacial energy, stabilizing slender columns. This is probed empirically via rate and temperature sweeps.
- Biaxial texture preservation at high rate: Maintain plume incidence symmetry and substrate temperature uniformity; slightly elevated pO2 (200–300 mTorr) mitigates Cu desorption at high growth flux. The multi-turn path allows multiple short exposures per pass, reducing thermal/mechanical gradients while reaching net high rates.
- Oxygenation: Two-step process (high pO2 cool + 450–500 °C anneal) achieves optimal δ while preserving interfacial oxygen-vacancy pinning at BSHO/EuBCO; variants will test the trade-off between Tc and vacancy-mediated pinning.

2) Microstructure and strain quantification
- Williamson–Hall: Collect FWHM for at least (005), (006), (007), (008) reflections; instrument broadening correction via standard Si powder. Linear fit yields ε (slope/4).
- TEM-GPA: Acquire HRTEM images across BSHO/EuBCO; compute in-plane strain maps εxx, εyy; derive dislocation density and Burgers vector content. Count dislocations per unit length at interfaces to verify “two edge dislocations per a-/b-axis per unit-cell mismatch” motif.
- STEM-EDS/EELS: Use probe-corrected STEM at 200–300 kV; map Sn M-, Hf M-, Ba L-, Cu K-, O K- edges. EELS O-K pre-peak intensity reduction near columns indicates local oxygen vacancy accumulation.

3) Transport and angular scaling
- Jc extraction: Four-probe I–V with voltage taps separated by 2–3 mm; 1 μV cm−1 criterion; correct for self-field at low B using standard methods.
- Fp scaling: Normalize Fp(B) to Fp,max; fit Dew-Hughes forms to extract p, q. Correlated c-axis pins typically shift Fp peak to higher b and produce strong c-axis Jc peaks; addition of random pinning broadens Fp(B) and suppresses saturation.
- Anisotropic GL scaling: Jc(θ,B,T) collapsed by Bε(θ) with ε(θ) = (cos2θ + γ−2 sin2θ)1/2; extract γ and deviations near c-axis peak to quantify correlated pin contribution.

D. Feasibility Assessment
- Equipment and availability:
  - R2R MPMT-PLD with ≥3 plumes and high-power excimer lasers is required; such systems are in operation in several REBCO labs and pilot lines.
  - High-field measurements up to 18 T are commonly available; 24–25 T access achievable via user facilities or partnering labs with cryogen-free or hybrid magnets.
  - TEM/STEM-EDS/EELS and XRD facilities are standard in materials research centers.
- Timeline (indicative):
  - Months 1–2: Target prep, PLD calibration, baseline growth.
  - Months 3–5: Co-doped optimization (ratio, rate, oxygenation).
  - Months 6–8: Full characterization (TEM, XRD, transport up to 18 T), first 24–25 T run.
  - Months 9–12: Ablations, thickness/rate sweeps, reproducibility along tape length, data consolidation.
- Resources/personnel:
  - 1 PLD process engineer, 1 TEM specialist, 1 transport measurement physicist, 1 data analyst/theorist, shared technicians.
- Risks and mitigations:
  - Risk: Texture degradation at ultra-high rate. Mitigation: Slightly higher pO2, maintain substrate T uniformity, reduce instantaneous flux by increasing number of plumes with lower per-plume rate.
  - Risk: Overgrowth/agglomeration of APCs at high loading. Mitigation: Cap total APCs at ≤10 mol%, include Sn:Hf ratio optimization to keep diameter ~5 nm.
  - Risk: Column splay >12°. Mitigation: Optimize plume incidence angle and substrate–plume geometry; ensure uniform in-plane template texture.
  - Risk: Oxygenation trade-offs. Mitigation: Controlled annealing series; track Tc vs Jc(B) to find optimum δ.

F. How the design validates conclusions
- Baselines (undoped, BSO-only, BHO-only) isolate the effects of each dopant on nucleation density, column diameter, and pinning, proving that the co-doped synergy is not achievable by either dopant alone.
- Ratio and rate sweeps test the mechanistic premise of differential diffusion (Sn fast/Hf slow): trends in column density and diameter vs Sn fraction and growth kinetics directly link microstructure to Jc(B,T,θ).
- Interface/strain characterization (TEM/EELS/GPA + Williamson–Hall) ties the presence of semi-coherent dislocations and oxygen-vacancy-rich zones to non-saturating Fp at high fields.
- Texture measurements ensure that high-rate growth does not compromise biaxial alignment, eliminating texture degradation as a confounding factor in Jc performance.
- Angular scaling and Dew-Hughes analysis distinguish correlated c-axis pinning from random pinning contributions, demonstrating the intended mixed pinning landscape.
- Reproducibility on multiple samples and along meter-length segments demonstrates process robustness and scalability.

G. Expected Outcomes and Decision Points
- Identify an optimal Sn:Hf ratio (near 4.5:3.5 mol%) that robustly yields ~5 nm-diameter BSHO columns at ~2200 μm−2 with Bφ ≈ 4.6–4.7 T, strong c-axis Jc peaks at intermediate fields, and non-saturating Fp up to 24–25 T at low temperature.
- If over-pinning reduces Jc anisotropy excessively or causes connectivity losses, reduce total APCs or increase stripe-like pure EuBCO regions by slight adjustments to growth temperature or oxygenation to interrupt columns, tuning vortex elasticity as needed.
- If texture degrades at the highest rate, operate at 60–100 nm s−1 where biaxial texture and column alignment remain optimal, still offering large throughput gains.

Notes on terminology (clarity):
- Artificial pinning centers (APCs): Second-phase nanoscale inclusions that pin magnetic vortices.
- Matching field (Bφ): Magnetic field equal to nΦ0, where n is areal density of columnar pins and Φ0 is the flux quantum; indicates field scale where each vortex can occupy a pin.
- Semi-coherent interface: Interface with periodic misfit dislocations allowing partial lattice matching without forming amorphous layers.
- Micro-strain: Average lattice strain derived from XRD peak broadening; reflects defect/strain fields that can pin vortices.
